1	# Leads
2	
3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine sends a daily (and monthly) gas nomination as a Word attachment to the HPL scheduler. Several Enron staff are copied, and someone has to re-key the volumes and confirm them back.: The same 'Calpine Daily Gas Nomination' email with 'CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc' arrives near-daily from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001. The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

Several Enron staff are copied, and someone has to re-key the volumes and confirm them back.: The same 'Calpine Daily Gas Nomination' email with 'CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc' arrives near-daily from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001. The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. content.content:
85	- New policies that add manual steps for book admins: a before/after minibook for every deal change, John Lavorato's approval for top-level adjustments, and a fixed leg order for Gas Daily four-leg deals so confirms work: These are stated as policies because communication between groups failed. Each one is manual work that systems could enforce or produce automatically. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/568.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/567.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/565.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/615.eml
86	- WeaponX Access database bloat: book admins must compact it by hand every week: The databases grow from about 12 to 30 MB up to 400 to 520 MB because data is imported and deleted daily. Greg Couch asks every book admin to compact manually, which a scheduled job could do. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/596.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/585.eml
87	- Monthly OPM (Operations Pricing Model) hours survey of activity hours by cost center: There are company-wide rollouts, reminders and Access installs. Managers like Daren Farmer could not get Access and sent spreadsheets instead, followed by clarification emails. It is described as a recurring monthly survey. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1436.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1445.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1447.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1437.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1400.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1384.eml
88	- Annual budget build: staffing worksheets, salary estimates, training and questionnaires collected by Diane Cook: There are several reminders and resends. Managers don't know their staff's salaries, so Diane collects estimates from each of them by hand, and returns come in late. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1392.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1399.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1401.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1409.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/791.eml
89	- Monthly and quarterly explanations of wholesale volume variances for Investor Relations: This is an explicit recurring monthly request ('It's that time again') to explain every change of 10% or more across many desk contacts. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1416.eml
90	- Requests for P&L support and top sheets, and the hand-off to a new controller: Requests go out to controllers, then on to book admins, with second requests. When roles change, requesters are pointed to new people by email each time. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/583.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/574.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/550.eml
91	- Pipeline and meter maintenance notices emailed to schedulers, plus follow-up 'back up' messages: Schedulers relay notices from PG&E, Duke and Gas Control to a list of 20 people one by one, then forward them again when the work ends. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1786.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1793.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1816.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1405.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1418.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1419.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1396.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1430.eml
92	- Replacing a meter (and its related facility changes) through a five-step sequence of manual system changes and phone calls across groups: Clem Cernosek's plan has people calling each other between steps and changing POPS by hand because the changes 'can not be done automatically'. Usage tickets can only be set for about 3 months, so one arrangement needed 7 tickets. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1439.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1442.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1444.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1796.eml
93	- Monthly first-of-month gas volume and nomination emails (Methanol/MTBE plants, Swift, Forest Oil) forwarded to traders and schedulers: The same message is sent every month and forwarded on. Revisions are sent separately, and deal end dates are not reflected in Sitara. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1423.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1424.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1467.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1393.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1422.eml
94	- Pipeline imbalance reconciliation and too many transport contracts: Ed Gottlob lists dozens of open imbalances, asks for contract netting, and calls the imbalance report 'pretty sad' (columns don't add up). He also asks for a curtailment-priority customer list for the Railroad Commission to be pulled from the contract system. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1433.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1470.eml
95	- Reconciling origination, monetized-deal waterfall payments and deals with counterparties or affiliates (New Power, Wisconsin Electric, Mary Lynne Ruffer's volumes): There are repeated chases ('Dave is wanting his money', 'Any word?'). A deal number changed with a book rename and broke the monetization tracking downstream. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/677.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/675.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/643.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/625.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/629.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/626.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1461.eml
96	- Access and security approvals (SRRS, TDS book access, Sitara desk access): Managers approve access requests by email links. TDS security approvals are being handed from one person to the desks, and access is requested by hand whenever a role changes. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1407.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/578.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/618.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/568.eml
97	- Updating contact and phone lists by hand, and sending org/role announcements: An assistant gathers each person's numbers by email. Risk contacts and counterparty phone changes are re-sent by email, and admin realignments are announced to large lists. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/646.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/660.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1380.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1459.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1465.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1432.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1443.eml
98	- Performance review (PRC) cycle administration and reminders: HR sends schedule and reminder emails to over 50 managers, and managers send in reviewer lists by email. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3219.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/790.eml
99	- Large volume of personal chain email and video forwarding through company mail: Dozens of forwards from one user, including MPEG/AVI attachments, political chain letters and offensive jokes, sent to internal and external lists. This costs storage and time and carries compliance risk. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/670.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/668.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/667.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/663.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/662.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/659.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/658.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/647.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/642.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/628.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/599.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/612.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/559.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/576.eml
100	- Logistics schedulers (Mary Poorman, Aimee Lannou, Jackie Young, Susan Hadix, Thu Nguyen) email the Texas desk (Daren Farmer) one by one to extend or create deals when gas flowed at a meter with no deal or nomination, so they can clear allocation exceptions or the 'UA4 list': A steady stream of nearly identical one-off requests (meter, days, last deal number, please extend), often about volumes of only a few Dth. Some go back to 1999. Each needs contract checks (Julie Meyers) and several rounds of replies. Flow on the first days after a shut-in, or valves not closed by 9am, keeps causing the same exception. This could be detected and given a default deal rule or strangers-gas rule automatically. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1478.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1479.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1482.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1480.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1483.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1487.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1486.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1489.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1492.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1493.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1502.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1508.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1512.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1520.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1522.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1543.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1544.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1559.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1560.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1960.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1982.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1983.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1987.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1999.eml
101	- Enerfin/TETCO meter 98-0439 volumes reallocated over and over between HPL, the East desk and Volume Management (retro deal extensions, OBA effective-date changes, Unify paths): Victor Lamadrid: 'We go round and round at this point changing volumes two, three or more times', and 'how often Enerfin's numbers change'. Long threads with many people over volumes of 9–141 Dth. HPL and TETCO allocation numbers don't match. The OBA date was changed retroactively without telling anyone. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1967.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1971.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1972.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1977.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1981.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2003.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1489.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1493.eml
102	- Approving write-offs of strangers gas to Unaccounted for Gas with a paper form (Clem Cernosek emails a form; the desk must print, sign and return the original): Many near-identical emails, one per meter, often for tiny or very old volumes (26 Mmbtu from 1999). Each needs a manual print-sign-return approval. This is a clear candidate for a batch or electronic approval workflow. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1499.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1961.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1963.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1973.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1974.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1975.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1978.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1985.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1986.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1988.eml
103	- Moving Canadian (ECC) deals booked in US books to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book; Stacey Vallejo sends deal IDs one at a time and invoicing waits until they're moved: This keeps happening (Nov 1, Nov 27 and Dec 6–8 requests). Invoicing for ECC and ENA is held up each month. Darron forwards each request on to book admins by hand. A booking validation rule could stop it at the source. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/539.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/535.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/460.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/459.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/419.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/406.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/405.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/404.eml
104	- Arthur Andersen monthly gas testing: pulling P&L top sheets and curve shift reports for the top five days, book by book: Requests come in month after month (August, September, October, Q3 close-out) and are passed down to book admins to pull together and photocopy. This could be a standard report that is generated automatically. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/516.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/515.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/420.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/517.eml

- Year-end performance reviews (PRC), development plans, signed paper review copies, and training module follow-ups.: A recurring HR cycle with chasing emails and signed paper originals. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/368.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/306.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/271.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/311.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/319.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2059.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2011.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/211.eml
- TDS and PortCalc book setup and maintenance: mapping TAGG books and region codes for new desks, manually setting the TDS position flag, and re-running and officializing books after deals move so credit data isn't duplicated.: Manual configuration steps with known failure modes ('since not everyone will do #1'). - Manually booking a complex virtual storage deal. Richard Tomaski states that the risk systems cannot handle it without a lot of manual manipulation, including volume adjustments weekly or monthly.: An explicitly recurring manual adjustment burden for the life of the deal. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/205.eml
- Purchase order and invoice receipt confirmation by email (AP and procurement asking whether goods were received).: Manual follow-up emails to close POs that are still open. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/252.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/237.eml
- Handing over Texas off-system pipeline rate maintenance and transport contract rate questions (moving the work to a new team).: Manual rate upkeep being moved between teams; a terminated contract required re-confirming rates. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2097.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2098.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2022.eml
- Credit Report forwarding: the credit group (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond, Jason Williams, Darren Vanek) sends a 'Credit Report' to about 35 people every day. It lists TAGG deals to rebook to the correct legal entity or to hold as 'Pending' for a credit officer. The West desk lead (Darron Giron) forwards each one by hand to a team member (Carole Frank, Pat Ryder or Ryan O'Rourke), who then fixes the deals. When he is away a week of these reports builds up and he forwards them all on his return.: There is one forward almost every business day from late February to May 2001, with the same mailing list each time. The reports show the same kinds of fixes again and again, such as Louis Dreyfus Holdings rebooked to Louis Dreyfus Corp, AEP Ltd rebooked to AEP Inc, and ENA rebooked to ECC 'under the ISDA'. This suggests the counterparty or entity mapping could be checked automatically when a deal is booked, and the reports could go straight to the right person. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/189.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/182.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/174.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/171.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/169.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/167.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/165.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/162.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/153.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/152.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/151.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/150.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/149.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/144.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/138.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/129.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/128.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/125.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/121.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/119.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/106.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/104.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/100.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/97.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/94.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/86.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/85.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/79.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/76.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/75.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/70.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/67.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/62.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/61.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/59.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/53.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/50.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/43.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/41.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/39.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/33.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/31.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/28.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/24.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/19.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/16.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/14.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/11.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/10.eml
- Moving Canadian-counterparty deals by hand: deals with Aquila Canada, Engage Energy Canada and TransCanada keep getting booked in Houston books between ENA and the counterparty. They have to be moved ('flipped') to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS (P&) book so that ECC settles them. Stacey Vallejo in Calgary finds them one at a time and asks the desk leads to search every book. Other one-off rebooks (W&T Offshore, RMT to ENA) are requested the same way.: There are many requests over two months. They say things like 'keep an eye out for deals with this company and flip them right away', 'I have a feeling that there are lots of deals like this in TAGG', and 'the EOL group is still working on a solution'. A bad booking forced February liquidations to be re-run and left deals missing from the April NYMEX invoice. The root cause is EOL/TAGG entity mapping, and the clean-up is manual. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/192.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/168.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/164.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/127.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/126.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/124.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/114.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/110.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/108.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/117.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/116.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/173.eml
- Meters with flow but no deal: when gas flows at a meter with no nomination, or its deal ticket has expired, schedulers and settlements email the trader (Daren Farmer) one meter at a time. They ask him to extend or create a deal ticket so that volumes can be allocated in Unify/MOPS and invoices drafted. Monthly transport-usage tickets also have to be re-created by hand each month.: Many separate emails show the same pattern, for example 'Meter 1351 has flow everyday for Feb', 'Can this deal be extended', 'Unable to draft volume in Unify due to the expired deal ticket', and 'This will help clear up some allocation exceptions'. A rule that flags or rolls over evergreen or recurring flows automatically could remove most of this. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2101.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2102.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2113.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2122.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2123.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2125.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2129.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/195.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/194.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/182.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/188.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/148.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/145.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/143.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/173.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2109.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2111.eml
- Price disputes between invoices and Sitara: settlements analysts (Katherine Herrera, Rebecca Griffin, Cynthia Hakemack, Genaro Mendoza, Scott Dozier, Charlene Richmond) find that a counterparty's invoice price differs from the price in Sitara. They email the trader or desk lead to confirm and change the price, often going through several people while an invoice deadline approaches. Some deals need a manual price update every month; deal 27253 is updated each month to whatever the customer invoices.: The pattern recurs across both mailboxes and many counterparties (TXU, Conoco, BP, Crosstex, Southern Union, Guadalupe, Cook, EnerVest). Typical lines are 'Customer invoiced ENA a price of...', 'Can you please update the deal in Sitara', and 'I need to send out my invoice this afternoon'. Index-based or formula prices (for example 'GDP DA -WACOG +.02') are being keyed in by hand as fixed rates. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2103.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/181.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/179.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/178.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/177.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/176.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/174.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/164.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/147.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/141.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/151.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2124.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/209.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/141.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/83.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/81.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/12.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/57.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/82.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/9.eml
- Monthly forward curve validation: Jennifer Nguyen reviews 10 curves each month and asks the desk leads to explain the large shifts. The leads in turn ask traders and reply, often with 'the market traded higher', which leads to more follow-up questions.: The same request arrives for January, February and March, each with a list of curves and reminders. The answers barely change, and Darron notes that 'this curve will probably show up every month'. A standard commentary or automatic market-data attribution could replace this round trip. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/170.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/133.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/132.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/49.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/48.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/47.eml
- Liquidation and flash support each month: Jim Little asks the desk leads for supporting detail behind the monthly liquidation values for each region. The detail is saved by hand to an ERMS/FRED Liquidations folder, and earlier months are chased again when they are missing.: The requests say 'I WILL ALSO NEED SUPPORT FOR THE DECEMBER AND JANUARY VALUES', followed by more requests for December Denver support and for March index deals. A bad booking also forced February liquidations to be re-run. The support is gathered the same way every month. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/187.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/163.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/105.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/168.eml
- Audit and data requests handled by email: Arthur Andersen asks for monthly gas-testing items (deal ticket, confirmation, forwards detail) and sends a quarterly testing checklist for the earnings release. Ad hoc requests also come in for MTM values by counterparty and for TAGG annuity values. Desk leads forward each request on to their staff.: The requests are monthly or quarterly, the checklist matrix covers every request so far, and requests get lost or delayed ('I was on vacation... didn't see it'). The forwarding chain runs from the desk lead to an analyst. Other requests in the same vein: 'Two more counterparties need MTM values', and 'For audit purposes, can you give us a brief description' of TAGG annuities. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/120.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/118.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/91.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/90.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/89.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/137.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/136.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/6.eml
- OA (operational accounting) and flash-to-actual variances: people investigate variances between flash/CPR figures and actual Unify/GL figures, for example on the PGEV park-and-lend imbalance and physical storage inventory. Gas Accounting has started a project to collect storage book codes and inventory schedules from every desk, and Risk has collected suggestions for improving OA.: Requests include 'it is causing an OA variance for us', 'Improvement in this process will help minimize flash-to-actual variances', and 'Has any progress been made on this?'. Darron admits 'I will see a variance that is rather small and just take it without looking into the underlying cause'. The variances come back every month. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2116.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/163.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/161.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/157.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/58.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/34.eml
- Monthly manual accounting for the GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap: every month someone has to zero out the HPL sale price to GLO, update the demand-charge tickets between HPL and ENA, and book the ENA sale to EGM at the value of the crude, all before flash.: Bryce Baxter writes that 'This will require the following steps be taken monthly' and 'This needs to be done monthly prior to flash'. A follow-up in April shows the bookings were still causing confusion. It is a clear candidate for an automated rule. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/175.eml
- Weekend on-call schedulers handle pipeline events (over- and under-deliveries, cuts, confirmation changes) and then write up manual 'On Call Notes' for the team. There is also a separate weekly systems-availability on-call email.: The notes follow the same format every weekend and record phone and pager handling plus manual confirmation changes in POPS. They are recurring operational overhead. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2110.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/210.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/180.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/167.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/26.eml
- Contract administration letters and reports: Cheryl Dudley produces a twice-monthly Assignment, Termination and Expiration Report by hand, and once forgot one ('accidentally failed to do the report for March'). Termination and shut-in notification letters need several people to work out the contract terms, such as whether a contract has evergreen language and what the letter should say.: The report is periodic and distributed by hand. Contract terms are stored inconsistently: the Global Contracts system said there was no evergreen clause, but the signed confirmation had one. This leads to email back-and-forth before each letter. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2114.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2119.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2120.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2121.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/172.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/171.eml
- Imbalance and balancing work: schedulers compile lists of points where gas is owed from the RTU variance and imbalance reports, track Oasis transport imbalances, and chase meter statements to find volumes missing from nominations (the Big Cowboy/GEPL overflow 'every month for at least the past six months'). King Ranch is consistently under-nominated.: 'We have an ongoing issue every month', 'we have consistently been under nominated', and an 'Urgent' request to compile a list by hand from spreadsheets. All of this points to recurring manual reconciliation. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2126.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2127.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2128.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/170.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/160.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/159.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/166.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/191.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/190.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/189.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/183.eml
- HPL sale to AEP: transition memos keep being redistributed, deal downloads are prepared for AEP, transport contracts are sorted between ENA and HPL, and new formal procedures are being drafted (counterparty maintenance, new books, employee security, curve mapping).: The issues memo is updated and resent over and over, and new recurring request processes are being defined. This is worth checking for duplicated effort. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2104.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/212.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/206.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/187.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/156.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/155.eml
- System access, user setup and book administration done by email: requests to add users to RiskTrac or GD_NEW uploads and the Canadian script, to add a Book Admin on the website, to move books under a trading group, to supply trader website access lists, and to count monitors. Darron asks that new hires have their applications and passwords ready when they start. Renaming the Denver books would mean changing every deal by hand.: There are many small one-off access requests. Darron's feedback says new-hire setup is a recurring pain, and the book rename 'will require a great deal of time and effort to change every deal'. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/157.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/156.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/140.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/18.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/15.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/63.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/92.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/131.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/102.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/130.eml
- Origination grants and credit reserves are recorded by hand: credit sends reserve memos, traders or originators ask for origination to be granted, and mistakes have to be corrected (a $100K double grant).: Requests and corrections are routed by email to the desk lead ('Sherry Dawson said you would probably be the one to grant this origination'). One grant was made twice by mistake. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/147.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/84.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/32.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/103.eml
- Penalty charges collected by survey: settlements emails about 25 analysts asking which counterparties invoiced or netted penalties for a production month, with a same-day deadline. A desk summary is then prepared for the head trader.: Each penalty amount, counterparty and deal is collected by hand across the whole group under a deadline ('I need this information before you leave today'). This could be a standing report. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/179.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/178.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/176.eml
- Daily approval by reply email: the prelim Enovate DPR (daily position report) is sent each day 'For your approval' and approved with an 'OK' reply.: It is a recurring daily approval sent by email, and could be approved in the system or by exception only. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/161.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/155.eml
- Nomination and deal-number exchange with customers and pipelines: Equistar's monthly nominations arrive late, and the scheduler needs deal numbers from the trader to confirm them. First-of-month noms (Swift, Duke Three Rivers), flexible Katy gas lists and maintenance outages are passed along by email. Oasis is moving to online nominations.: The same information is copied by hand at each first-of-month cycle. Oasis's online nom/confirm system is an automation opportunity mentioned in the mail itself. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/152.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/144.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/153.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/158.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/201.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/200.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/150.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/149.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/202.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2130.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2108.eml
- Matching SFAS 133 hedges by hand: offsetting third-party trades have to be identified and documented for internal Transwestern/RMTC hedges, about 97 trades found by hand at year end, with the work now repeating for new trades.: The email says 'More Deals', and the effectiveness testing cannot be done without the third-party positions. A $27MM earnings impact is at stake. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/71.eml
- Recurring HR and admin collection by email: lists of potential reviewers for mid-year reviews, PBA nominations, analyst and associate needs assessments, and topic lists for training sessions are each gathered by emailing every lead.: These are periodic people-process requests gathered by hand with deadlines and reminders ('I've received only one response so far'). Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/518.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/5.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/65.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/60.eml
- Failing internal tools: the Global Standards exception-reporting Access database and the training-approval website both give errors, and the PMA files and the physical template revision are handed around by hand.: Darron writes 'I get an error when I launch the program in Access' and 'I get an error when I try to approve this'. The exception database goes unused by the gas group. Files: corpus/giron-d/sent/74.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/135.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/185.eml, corpus/giron-d/sent/193.eml
- Monthly gas settlements chasing price differences: settlements staff (mostly Megan Parker, also Elizabeth Hernandez and Tess Ray) email the logistics lead (Daren Farmer) one deal at a time to check prices in Sitara against counterparty invoices. Counterparties include Mirant, Texaco, DEFS, Tristar, Duke, Houston Exploration, MGI, Global Octanes and Dow (Cowtrap/Blue Dolphin).: A steady stream of single-deal questions, each needing someone to look up the trader or the trader's deal book. Requests sit unanswered (Hernandez re-sent after 3 weeks). Amounts are large (Houston Expl. $222k, MGI $10.6k), and some deals belong to traders who have left (Danny Conner). Lee Papayoti could not edit an old Enron deal after the move to AEP. 	From:  Larry Joe Hunter                           02/08/2001 06:27 PM
	

To: Ellen Wallumrod/NA/Enron@ENRON, Jeffrey C Gossett/HOU/ECT@ECT, Kam 
Keiser/HOU/ECT@ECT, Phillip M Love/HOU/ECT@ECT, Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, 
Errol McLaughlin/Corp/Enron@ENRON, David Baumbach/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc:  
Subject: Audit Request procedure


Jeff, 
Thanks for the lead with Avril Forster, it looks like that will help us in 
the near future.  Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, 
we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market 
valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio.

Desk heads,

Can you provide to Ellen and myself the names of the person on your desk who 
we should go to with these requests.  Also, please let these persons know 
that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several 
per week).

Here's the background of these requests.  Because of various accounting 
rules, Parties dealing in Derivatives must show third party valuations to 
their Auditors.  Our group (Confirmations) is responsible for providing MTM 
values and open position reports for these parties.  We do not have access to 
any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line 
"EnTelligence" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us 
to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without 
having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book.

Thanks for the help.  We'll try to get these off of your plates as soon as 
possible.

Joe

content.thinking: I've confirmed the daily Credit Report forwards in giron-d/sent (about 65 of them, 1/24/01 to 5/9/01, with the same alias counterparties rebooked repeatedly). Sending that to the critic now, then moving on to the next leads.

input.prompt:
Proposal: route the daily Credit Report straight to each desk's book admin, and stop recurring rebooks with a counterparty legal-entity alias table at TAGG deal entry.

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
Every business day, Credit (Veronica Espinoza / Russell Diamond) emails a 'Credit Report' to about 35 people. It lists TAGG deals that must be rebooked to the correct legal entity or held 'Pending' for a credit officer. The West desk lead, Darron Giron, receives it and forwards each day's report by hand to his book admin, Carole Frank, who then rebooks the deals. Forwards sometimes go out in batches days late. Many of the rebooks are the same alias-to-entity corrections repeated on different days.

Evidence:
- The forward happens daily. giron-d/sent has a dated forward for almost every business day from 1/24/01 to 5/9/01, about 65 files, e.g. corpus/giron-d/sent/259.eml "Subject: Credit Report--1/24/01", 260.eml "Credit Report--1/25/01", 261.eml "Credit Report--1/26/01", 262.eml "Credit Report--1/29/01", 263.eml "Credit Report - 1/30/01", 264.eml "Credit Report--1/31/01" ... 10.eml "Credit Report--5/9/01". Each one starts "---------------------- Forwarded by Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT" and is addressed "To: carole.frank@enron.com".
- Late batch forwards: corpus/giron-d/sent/259.eml (report dated 01/24/2001) and 263.eml (report dated 01/30/2001) were both forwarded "on 02/02/2001".
- The same corrections recur:
  * Louis Dreyfus: corpus/giron-d/sent/263.eml "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings  qO0682.1  Rebook to Louis Dreyfus" (1/30/01); corpus/giron-d/sent/151.eml "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holding qX0857.1 Rebook to Louis Dreyfus Corporation" (3/15/01); corpus/giron-d/sent/149.eml "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings qX5624.1  Louis Dreyfus Corporation" (3/19/01).
  * PanCanadian: 263.eml "PanCanadian Energy Inc.   qO1735.1  Rebook to PanCanadian Energy Services," and 149.eml "PanCanadian Energy Inc.  qX4599.1  Rebook to PanCanadian Energy Services Inc." (three TAGG numbers that day).
  * El Paso: 151.eml "El Paso Gas Marketing Company qX0900.1.2      Rebook to El Paso Merchant" and 149.eml "El Paso Energy Corporation  qX5675.1  Rebook to El Paso Merchant Energy LP".
  * Canadian affiliates under the ISDA: 151.eml "Rebook ENA trades to ECC ( under" (TransCanada), 149.eml "Rebook ENA to ECC, under the ISDA" (PG&E Energy Trading, Canada), 14.eml "Engage Energy Canada LP  v78253.1  Rebook ENA trades to ECC (under the ISDA)".
- Report size: 263.eml (1/30/01) lists about 30 counterparty lines; 149.eml (3/19/01) about 20; 14.eml (5/7/01) 8.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
1. Credit adds each desk's book admin (for the West desk, Carole Frank) to the Credit Report distribution, or sorts the report by book/desk. This removes the desk lead's daily forward and the multi-day lag.
2. Credit and Global Counterparty keep an alias table, recording that a given short name (for example "Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings", "PanCanadian Energy Inc.", "El Paso Energy Corporation", or a Canadian affiliate with an ECC ISDA) must be booked to a specific legal entity. TAGG/EOL deal entry uses the table to default or block the entity, so these rebooks are never created.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
The book admin gets the report directly the same morning. Alias names that credit has already ruled on are booked correctly at entry, so the daily list shrinks to genuinely new counterparties and items pending a credit officer.

SAVINGS (estimates; please judge)
- Darron's forward: about 2 min per business day removed outright.
- Recurring alias rebooks avoided: across the report, about 3 rebook lines per day are repeats of an entity credit has already ruled on (Louis Dreyfus, PanCanadian, El Paso, AEP, ENA-to-ECC under the ISDA). At about 5 min per rebook (find the deal in TAGG, change the counterparty, re-check) for the book admin, that is about 15 min/day across desks. The alias table is maintained by credit, which already makes these rulings, so it moves no work onto anyone else.
- Total about 17 min per business day × 21 business days = about 357 min ≈ 6.0 hours/month ≈ $506/month at $85/h.
If you think the rebook-avoidance part is not supported well enough, please consider saving the forwarding/routing part on its own: 2 min × 21 = 42 min ≈ 0.7 h/month ≈ $60/month.

No email in these files tried to instruct the analyst.

# Saved

Nothing yet.

# Rejected

- Calpine daily gas nomination by emailed Word document: Have Calpine send its daily nomination through a structured feed or web form that loads into scheduling, and confirm only when volumes change.. Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. The re-keying, the daily phone call and the 'no change' confirmation that make up most of the 10 minutes are not shown; the confirmation rests on one undated message that does not match the rest of the archive. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.

input.prompt:
Proposal: replace the one-memo-per-meter, print-sign-return approval for HPL Strangers Gas write-offs with a monthly batch exception list, electronic approval, and an automatic write-off below a small volume threshold.

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
When gas flows at an HPL meter with no deal, POPS books it to the "HPL Strangers Gas Contract". Clem Cernosek (Logistics) researches each meter and types a memo per meter to Daren Farmer (Texas desk), listing days and MMBtu. Daren has to choose (1) extend a deal, (2) enter a new deal, or (3) approve a write-off to Unaccounted for Gas, and must print, sign and return the paper original. Bob Cotten then moves the volume to the write-off account by hand. Many memos are for tiny or very old volumes, and some need extra email rounds.

Evidence:
- Template and paper step: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2002.eml (12/21/00, meter 986631): "Currently, these volumes are being booked under the HPL Strangers Gas Contract.  Logistics needs either (1)  have Deal #120891 extended, (2) new deal, or (3) approval to writeoff these volumes to Unaccounted for Gas.  (Please print, sign, and return original to Clem Cernosek)."
- Earlier instance: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1499.eml (11/7/00): "On 1/5/99, the above meter recorded flow 1,703 Mmbtus." ... "Please print, approve, and return original to me."
- Tiny, old volumes: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1346.eml (8/18/00, meter 985355) lists ten days from 3/30/99 to 7/31/00 with entries such as "8/3/99    5" and "10/29/99   5", totalling "203".
- Manual move afterwards: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2045.eml (Bob Cotten, 1/12/01): "The total volume of 1,517 mmbtu that flowed during the period of 12/1/99 through 3/31/00 has been moved from the Strangers Gas Contract to 012-41500-02-004 for write-off purposes." The memo it answers says "(Please print, sign, and return the original to Clem Cernosek)."
- Extra rounds: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1963.eml: Daren "What was going on in Feb?", Clem forwards "Please response.", and Aimee Lannou explains.
- Volume of memos: there is a separate Clem memo per meter on almost every business day between 12/11/00 and 1/9/01, 24 files in all: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1961, 1973, 1974, 1975, 1978, 1985, 1986, 1988, 2002, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2024, 2027, 2033, 2034, 2036 (.eml), with subjects like "HPL Meter #981488 PARIS TENASKA HPL" (2016) and "HPL Meter #984179 HOFF-HELLER UNIT #22 CDP" (2020). Earlier ones exist in Aug and Nov 2000 (1346, 1499).

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
1. POPS/Unify produces a monthly exception report of all volumes sitting on the Strangers Gas contract, by meter and day, with the last deal at the meter. This replaces Clem typing each memo.
2. Below a threshold (for example under 100 MMBtu on a meter in a month), volumes are written off to UA4 automatically under a standing approval from the desk lead.
3. Larger items go to Daren as one list each month, approved electronically line by line (extend deal X / new deal / write off). There is no printing, and no paper original routed back.
4. The approved list drives the move to the write-off account in a batch, not one meter at a time.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
Once a month, the desk lead reviews one list, ticks a decision per line, and logistics runs the write-offs in one batch. Tiny items never reach him.

SAVINGS (estimate)
Per memo today: Clem compiling and typing about 10 min, Daren printing, signing and returning the original about 5 min, and Bob Cotten's individual move about 5 min, so about 20 min. With the batch list and threshold, about 5 min per item remains (review on a list, batch move). Saving about 15 min per item.
Frequency: 24 memos in the four weeks 12/11/00–1/9/01 (above). Call it 20 per month. 20 × 15 = 300 min = 5.0 hours/month ≈ $425/month at $85/h.
(If you judge that the Dec–Jan burst was a year-end cleanup rather than the normal rate, a lower rate, say 10 per month, gives 2.5 h ≈ $213/month.)

No email in these files tried to instruct the analyst.

cc:  
Subject: WeaponX

I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the 
following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already).

Open the database while holding down on the shift key.  This will open the 
database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
can use the database as normal.

Just a quick explanation:

This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.

The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one 
for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB.  You can see that we will save 
several GB if everyone begins compacting the databases on a regular basis.

Please note:  Even though this is standard Access procedure, I would 
recommend that the book admin save a copy of their existing WeaponX file 
prior to compacting for the first time.  Once the file is compacted and a 
daily run has been successful, they can delete the backup file.  It is not 
necessary for them to save a backup copy each time before compacting.  I am 
only recommending it for the first compact.

I don't anticipate any problems with this procedure.  As a matter of fact, 
Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily 
basis.  In addition Ann (West desk) ran a test for me with no problems.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Greg

Proposal: replace the manual weekly compaction of the WeaponX Access databases by book admins with an automatic compact (Access "Compact on Close", or a scheduled overnight job).

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
WeaponX is an Access database that each desk's book admin runs daily. Because it imports and deletes data every day, the file bloats to hundreds of MB. Greg Couch asked every desk's book admins to compact it by hand at least once a week. They hold Shift while opening it, choose Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database, then wait for the compaction to finish before using it. Desk leads forwarded the instruction to their admins.

Evidence:
- corpus/giron-d/sent/596.eml (Greg Couch, 10/13/2000, to Gossett, Etter, Kelly, Baumbach, Giron and Keiser, forwarded by Darron Giron to Anne Bike): "I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already)." ... "Open the database while holding down on the shift key." ... "choose Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you can use the database as normal." ... "WeaponX imports and deletes a lot of data on a daily basis." ... "The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB." ... "Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily basis."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/585.eml (10/17/2000): Giron forwards the same instruction again to Anne Bike, "Try this and see if it does any good." This suggests the database was causing trouble and the step was being pushed again.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
The WeaponX owner (Greg Couch) turns on Access's "Compact on Close" option in the WeaponX file, or adds a scheduled overnight compact-and-repair job for each desk's copy. Book admins no longer do anything.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
Each file is compacted automatically every day. Admins open WeaponX normally, and file sizes stay around the 12–30 MB seen after compaction.

SAVINGS (estimate)
Per manual compaction: about 10 min of book admin time (open with Shift, run the compact on a 400–520 MB file and wait, reopen, check the daily run). The memo went to six desk leads, so at least six book admins (one per desk; some desks have more) × once a week = 6 × 4.3 = about 26 compactions a month. 26 × 10 min = 260 min ≈ 4.3 hours/month ≈ $368/month at $85/h. The one-time setup is a few minutes for the owner. Admins like Crystal who compact daily would save more.

No email in these files tried to instruct the analyst.

9	- Calpine daily gas nomination by emailed Word document: Have Calpine send its daily nomination through a structured feed or web form that loads into scheduling, and confirm only when volumes change.. Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. The re-keying, the daily phone call and the 'no change' confirmation that make up most of the 10 minutes are not shown; the confirmation rests on one undated message that does not match the rest of the archive. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
10	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded it in `decisions.md`. The problem is how often the work happens, not whether the quotes are accurate.

**What holds up:** Every quote and file checks out. All 24 files from 12/11/00 to 1/9/01 are memos from Clem Cernosek to Daren Farmer about Strangers Gas volumes, and nearly all ask him to "print, sign, and return original". 1346 and 1499 are earlier memos of the same kind, 2045 shows Bob Cotten moving the volume by hand, and 1963 shows the extra email rounds.

**Why it fails:** The estimated 20 memos a month (or the fallback of 10) is not supported. The December–January burst was a one-time cleanup of very old volumes, not the normal pace:
- The memos clear volumes mostly from 1999. For example, 1975 is for 101 MMBtu that flowed on 4/18/99, 2024 is for 10 MMBtu from 6/16/99, and 2045 covers 12/1/99–3/31/00.
- Before the burst there is only one memo in August 2000 (1346) and one in November 2000 (1499).
- After 1/9/01 there are none. The last related message is 2040 on 1/9/01, and 2045 on 1/12/01 only closes out an earlier memo. This is not a gap in the archive: more than 200 messages in the same folder are dated February to June 2001, and the mail runs to October 2001.

So the steady rate is about one memo every couple of months at most. At that rate, building a monthly exception report and a standing approval to write off gas automatically would save little. The automatic write-off would also need sign-off as a financial control, and the proposal doesn't address that.

**What could change the verdict:** Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or found in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), showing the work kept recurring at a steady monthly rate. Without that, a cleanup that has ended can't be presented as recurring work.

The rejection is in `C:/Users/camta/Desktop/camilo-aictualize-project/out/workspaces/analyst-6/proposals/strangers-gas-writeoff-reject.json`.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because it duplicates one that's already saved. The idea and the evidence are both sound, but the managers already have this exact work and change in front of them.

**Why it's a duplicate:** `decisions.md` already lists "Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests" as saved item 1, at $1,694.05 a month. It proposes the same thing: a read-only report that lets Confirmations value a counterparty's deals across all desks as of a past date. It cites giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240 and 241, which include all four messages this proposal uses. `check` flagged it too: all 3 of its occurrences are already occurrences of that saved proposal. Two earlier versions of the same idea have also been rejected for the same reason.

**The claims themselves hold up:**
- All quotes match the mail.
- Treating "we recieve several per week" in 241.eml as 3 a week (13 a month) is reasonable.
- `check` got the same figures: 54 minutes × 13 a month = 11.7 hours, or $994.50 a month.

Two small points if anyone reworks the saved version:
- The 137.eml request was sent by Jeffrey Gossett to the other desk heads, not by Confirmations.
- In 241.eml, Joe Hunter thanks Gossett for "the lead with Avril Forster", which he says "will help us in the near future". That suggests some fix was already under way.

Neither changes the verdict. More research would not change it either; only new work not covered by the saved proposal would, so `research` is null.

summary:
I rejected this proposal because it duplicates one that's already saved. The idea and the evidence are both sound, but the managers already have this exact work and change in front of them.

**Why it's a duplicate:** `decisions.md` already lists "Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests" as saved item 1, at $1,694.05 a month. It proposes the same thing: a read-only report that lets Confirmations value a counterparty's deals across all desks as of a past date. It cites giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240 and 241, which include all four messages this proposal uses. `check` flagged it too: all 3 of its occurrences are already occurrences of that saved proposal. Two earlier versions of the same idea have also been rejected for the same reason.

**The claims themselves hold up:**
- All quotes match the mail.
- Treating "we recieve several per week" in 241.eml as 3 a week (13 a month) is reasonable.
- `check` got the same figures: 54 minutes × 13 a month = 11.7 hours, or $994.50 a month.

Two small points if anyone reworks the saved version:
- The 137.eml request was sent by Jeffrey Gossett to the other desk heads, not by Confirmations.
- In 241.eml, Joe Hunter thanks Gossett for "the lead with Avril Forster", which he says "will help us in the near future". That suggests some fix was already under way.

Neither changes the verdict. More research would not change it either; only new work not covered by the saved proposal would, so `research` is null.

Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only report that values a counterparty's deals across all desks as of a past date, so Risk analysts no longer do it by hand. ($298.35 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/108.eml, giron-d/sent/114.eml, giron-d/sent/195.eml, giron-d/sent/270.eml, giron-d/sent/292.eml, giron-d/sent/360.eml, giron-d/sent/539.eml, giron-d/sent/550.eml
6	4. Monthly roll of Sitara transport usage tickets: A month-end job extends each active usage ticket, fills its rate from the matrix/Unify rates and carries last month's volume, leaving people only an exception list. ($198.05 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1144.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1145.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1257.eml, farmer-d/logistics/867.eml
7	
8	# Rejected
9	
10	- Calpine daily gas nomination by emailed Word document: Have Calpine send its daily nomination through a structured feed or web form that loads into scheduling, and confirm only when volumes change.. Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. The re-keying, the daily phone call and the 'no change' confirmation that make up most of the 10 minutes are not shown; the confirmation rests on one undated message that does not match the rest of the archive. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
11	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill managers' monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys from ATEs/SAP and system reports so managers only correct exceptions.. Why: The organization had already built most of this: from late 2000 the Access hours survey carries forward commercial teams and FTEs and shows prior-month hours, and the driver survey already let groups send a standard report instead. The proposal mistakes a one-off January 2001 SAP glitch for the normal monthly process, and hours by activity cannot be taken from ATEs/SAP. Research that could settle it: Find what managers still do by hand each month in the Access tool after the January 2001 SAP changeover (for example, splitting hours by activity and team, as in 84.eml), how long it takes, and whether any driver surveys were still sent after August 2000; then size only that remaining work.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
14	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
15	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry.. Why: The swap covered only January to May 2001 and its bookings were done as a one-time cleanup months later, not as monthly work, so there is no ongoing work for the change to save.
16	- Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests: Finish EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios without routing requests through the Risk desks.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
17	- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
18	- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
19	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
20	- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
21	- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. I rejected this proposal because it's a duplicate. Another critic has already saved the same work as item 2 in `decisions.md`: "Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases", at $368.05 a month. It cites the same two messages, `giron-d/sent/585.eml` and `giron-d/sent/596.eml`, and proposes the same nightly automatic compaction. `check` refused to save it again for that reason.

The problem is duplication, not the idea or the evidence. More research won't change that, so there's nothing to fix. Searching the mail for other WeaponX messages turned up nothing that would make this a separate piece of work.

If anyone revisits the saved item, three points in this version are worth checking:
- **Minutes per compaction:** 10 is likely too high. After the first compaction, a weekly compaction runs on a file that has grown for only a week from about 12–30 MB, not on a 400–520 MB file. About 5 minutes of the admin's time, mostly waiting, is more realistic. At that figure the saving is about $184 a month, not $368.
- **"Desk leads forwarded the instruction to their admins":** the mail only shows Darron Giron forwarding it, to Anne Bike, on 10/13 and again on 10/17. Nothing shows the other five leads forwarding it.
- **"Try this and see if it does any good":** it hints that Anne had a problem, but it doesn't show the database was causing trouble.

I split your proposal in two. I saved the forwarding part on its own at a smaller figure, and rejected the alias-table part.

**Saved: forwarding the daily Credit Report** (entry 6 in `decisions.md`, about $25 a month)
- **Forwards counted:** Darron Giron's sent mail has 71 Credit Report forwards to Carole Frank, covering the reports from 1/24/01 to 5/9/01, not about 65.
- **Who gets the report:** Carole is not on Credit's mailing list, even as late as 5/9/01 (`10.eml`). Darron's own list of book admins names her as Frank Ermis's book admin (`1.eml`). So adding her to the list removes the forward.
- **Minutes:** I cut the time to 1 minute per forward. Each forward goes out with no added comment, so 2 minutes is generous. The check counts the rate from the 71 forwards: 17.5 a month, about 0.3 hours a month.
- **Late forwards:** I left the batch forwards on 2/2/01 out as a "stall". They look more like Darron catching up on missed reports than like work being held up, and nothing in the mail shows any harm from the delay.

**Rejected: the alias table for repeat rebooks**
This is a problem with the evidence, not the idea. Two earlier versions combining rebooks and forwarding were already rejected in `decisions.md` (items 19 and 23) for the same gaps:
- **No mail on the rebook work:** none shows who rebooks the deals, how long a rebook takes, or which report lines belong to the West desk. The report goes to every desk, so the 15 minutes a day for Carole is a guess.
- **The mappings are not fixed:** on 1/30/01 Aquila Energy Gas Marketing is rebooked to Utilicorp United (`263.eml`). On 3/19/01 Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management Corp. (`149.eml`). The same report lists "AEP Energy Services, Inc. ... Rebook to AEP Energy Services, Inc.", so one of your example aliases maps to itself. A fixed table would book some of these wrong.

**Research that could settle it:**
1. Count the rebook lines across all 71 reports and keep only the counterparties that always go to the same entity.
2. Find mail showing who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Julie Brewer's "Can you please have this deal rebooked as indicated by credit" in `124.eml` is a starting point.
3. Count only the West desk's lines.

Proposal: replace one-meter-at-a-time "please extend this deal" emails to the Texas desk with an automatic nightly flow-without-active-deal exception list, plus a pre-expiry alert for deals at meters that are still flowing.

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
When gas flows at an HPL meter after its Sitara deal has expired (or a deal lapsed because the evergreen flag was wrong, or there is overflow for a day or two), the volume lands on allocation exceptions or on Strangers Gas. Then a volume-management, logistics or settlements person researches the last deal at that meter and emails the desk lead, Daren Farmer, about that single meter. Daren decides, extends or creates the deal (sometimes after asking contracts or a trader), and replies. Some threads take several rounds. Requests come from many people (Jackie Young, Aimee Lannou, Mary Poorman, Michael Olsen, Karen Lindley, Tom Acton, Katherine Herrera), all year.

Evidence (quotes):
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1029.eml (Jackie Young, 4/10/00): "Here I go again...................." / "98-6373, Sitara deal #128952 expired 3/31/2000." / flows of ".461 decatherms" etc. / "Help?"
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1021.eml (Jackie Young, 4/6/00): "I hate to be a pest but here's the deal on the above two meters:" ... "There is no   new deal referenced, nor is the evergreen flag in effect." ... "this meter is active   monthly and I'm thinking that it will flow for this month with no K being applied."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/899.eml (3/10/00): "Can you please check into whether or not the below deals for the above meters can be rolled and extended?" Daren replies "I extended the deal at mtr 6719 to include 2/10." Jackie then has to route the K # to Anita Luong for an accounting arrangement.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1406.eml (9/13/00): Aimee "can you get a deal set up for meter 6879 for Sept. 00?". Daren forwards to Julie Meyers: "The deal shows evergreen, but nothing rolled to September." Julie: "This deal was not put in right."
- Jan–Feb 2001, one email per meter:
  * 2030.eml (1/5/01): "There was flow at meter 1351 for Dec 2000.  It flowed every day" ... "it is currently on stranger's gas."
  * 2031.eml (1/5/01): "there is flow at meter 1386 for Jan 1-3."
  * 2038.eml (1/9/01): "meter 5192 flowed 8 dth on 12/19, 33 dth on 12/20 and 2 dth on 12/29." ... "Could you please extend this deal for these 3 days or create a new one?"
  * 2047.eml (1/17/01, Karen Lindley): "there was overflow from November  on meter 985097 and the following deals need to be extended for 12/1 only."
  * 2049.eml (1/22/01): "Deal 150325 expired on day 3.  Could you please extend this deal or create a new one?"
  * 2052.eml (1/24/01, Michael Olsen, deal 502952) and its follow-up 2078.eml (2/5/01): "For Dec. and Jan. production there are flow volumes without a deal.  Deal 502952 was good for November."
  * 2077.eml (2/5/01, Mary Poorman): "the deal to sell to San Jac is expired.  Do you want me to extend the deal to cover the volume?"
  * 2082.eml (2/14/01): "that deal was only good for Dec."
  * 2092.eml (2/23/01): "The above meter recorded a flow on Jan 15 this year." ... "Do we need to put in a deal for this flow?"
  * 2093/2095.eml (2/23/01, meter 6884): "wondering if deals 137870 and 235670 needed to be extended into 2001", then "Deal with inactive or suspended counterparty may not be extended." / "Any suggestions?"
- Settlements is blocked too: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/194.eml (4/4/01): "This deal has expired for Teco Gas Processing, but we did have a sale in 02/01. Should this deal be extended?" ... "Unable to draft volume in Unify due to the expired deal ticket". corpus/farmer-d/logistics/148.eml (5/7/01, Tom Acton): "I need  deal ticket 745546 extended on both ends." ... "This will help clear up some allocation exceptions."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
1. A nightly POPS/Sitara job lists every meter-day with measured flow and no active deal. For each it shows the last deal at the meter, its counterparty, trader and end date, and whether the evergreen flag was set. The list goes to the desk lead and to volume management as one report.
2. Five business days before month end, an alert lists deals that are expiring at meters that flowed in the last 30 days, so they can be extended or deliberately ended before the gas lands on exceptions.
3. The desk lead marks each line (extend / new deal / zero-volume extension / write off), and volume management actions it from the list. This replaces the individual research-and-email by the requester and the individual reply.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
Most lapses are caught before month end by the pre-expiry alert. Any that slip through appear on the next morning's list with the research already done. One reviewer clears them in a batch, with no separate emails, chasers or forwards.

SAVINGS (estimate)
Per item today: the requester looks up the last deal and counterparty and writes the email (about 8 min), Daren reads, decides, extends and replies (about 5 min), and about half need a further round with contracts, a trader or settlements (about 6 min average). Total about 19 min.

Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
15	- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.
16	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill managers' monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys from ATEs/SAP and system reports so managers only correct exceptions.. Why: The organization had already built most of this: from late 2000 the Access hours survey carries forward commercial teams and FTEs and shows prior-month hours, and the driver survey already let groups send a standard report instead. The proposal mistakes a one-off January 2001 SAP glitch for the normal monthly process, and hours by activity cannot be taken from ATEs/SAP. Research that could settle it: Find what managers still do by hand each month in the Access tool after the January 2001 SAP changeover (for example, splitting hours by activity and team, as in 84.eml), how long it takes, and whether any driver surveys were still sent after August 2000; then size only that remaining work.
17	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
18	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
19	- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry..
