21	- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
22	- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
23	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
24	- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
25	- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240, 241, plus 136).
26	- Weekly manual compact of WeaponX databases: Compact each desk's WeaponX file automatically every night instead of having each book admin do it by hand every week.. Why: The same work and change is already saved in decisions.md as item 2, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml).
27	- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Block known wrong-entity counterparties at TAGG deal entry with a credit-kept 'use instead' mapping, and route each Credit Report row to the owning book administrator.. Why: The 65 minutes a day rests on a 'fixed mapping' that the mail contradicts (the Aquila/Utilicorp rebook runs in opposite directions, the Louis Dreyfus target changes, and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself), on a repeat rate of half when the cited reports show about a third, and on six desk heads forwarding every day when only Giron's forwards, often sent days late in batches, appear in the mail. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs that always have the same target. Find mail from book administrators or Confirmations, such as Julie Brewer's chase in 124.eml, that shows who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Check whether desk heads other than Giron forward the report at all, given that the book administrators are already on its distribution list.
28	- Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX databases: Have WeaponX compact itself automatically (scheduled overnight compact or Compact on Close) so book admins stop doing it by hand.. Why: The same work, citing the same two messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases'.
29	- Monthly search and flip of ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Auto-book ECC master-swap counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS at entry (EOL rule plus TAGG default) and send a nightly exception list to book owners.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/108, 114, 270, 292, 360).
30	- Rebooking deals to the right legal entity from the daily Credit Report: Add a credit-maintained alias table in TAGG that books known wrong entities to the approved one, and route each day's remaining exceptions by book instead of a desk lead forwarding the whole report. Why: The mail contradicts the fixed wrong-to-right pairs the alias table depends on (the same entity is sent to different targets, and Aquila/Utilicorp are rebooked in both directions), and the 9 minutes a day of West-desk rebooks, which make up half the savings, are not supported by anything in the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk's books and how long a rebook takes, and check across all the reports whether each wrong entity always goes to the same target (only about 10 of the ~70 forwarded reports have the list in the message body).
31	- Recurring alias-to-entity rebooks from the daily Credit Report: Credit and Global Counterparty keep an alias table that TAGG/EOL deal entry uses to default or block the legal entity, so repeat rebooks are never created.. Why: No mail shows who does the rebooks, how long each one takes, or that about 3 repeat lines a day belong to any one desk. The mappings are not fixed either: Aquila is rebooked to Utilicorp United on 1/30/01 (263.eml) but Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management on 3/19/01 (149.eml), and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is 'rebooked' to itself (149.eml). So 15 minutes a day is a guess. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs whose target never changes. Then find mail from book admins or Confirmations (for example Julie Brewer's 'Rebooks' request in 124.eml) showing who rebooks, how long a rebook takes and which lines are the West desk's.
32	- Routing daily Credit Report rebooks to book admins and checking legal entity at deal entry: Credit splits the daily Credit Report by TAGG book and sends each book's lines only to that book's admin, and TAGG/EOL warns or defaults to the legal entity that holds the master agreement when a deal is entered.. Why: The forwarding part is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md and cites the same 71 Giron forwards. The rest repeats claims that earlier critics rejected: no mail shows the other five desk heads forwarding or any admin scanning the list, and the entity mappings the entry check needs change from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail from desk heads other than Giron, or from book admins or Confirmations, showing them forwarding the report, picking out their own lines, or rebooking, and how long that takes. Then count, across all 71 reports, the counterparty pairs whose target entity never changes, and size only that.
33	- Self-service counterparty MTM report for audit confirmation requests: Give Confirmations a back-dated counterparty MTM / open-position report (EnTelligence with back-dated curves) so audit requests no longer go to every Risk desk head and analyst.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests' (decisions.md item 1), which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).

# Rejected

- Calpine daily gas nomination by emailed Word document: Have Calpine send its daily nomination through a structured feed or web form that loads into scheduling, and confirm only when volumes change.. Why: The mail only shows Calpine emailing a .doc to the scheduler with Enron staff copied. The re-keying, the daily phone call and the 'no change' confirmation that make up most of the 10 minutes are not shown; the confirmation rests on one undated message that does not match the rest of the archive. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the HPL schedulers (Lloyd, Lannou, Farmer) showing what they do with the Calpine .doc, such as typing it into a nomination system, replying to confirm, or fixing errors. Also check whether Calpine would agree to a new format and how many nominations a month actually arrive.
- Calpine daily gas nomination intake: Replace Calpine's emailed Word-document nomination, phone call and confirm reply with a structured feed that loads into scheduling and acknowledges itself automatically.. Why: The savings rest on steps the mail does not show: phone calls appear in only 5 of 22 Calpine nominations and Calpine says it calls only for changes, no HPL scheduler confirmation reply exists (the one cited is an undated internal note by Darron Giron, who is not the scheduler), and weekend nominations come in one Friday email, so 30 per month at 14 minutes each is overstated. Research that could settle it: Find HPL scheduler replies or confirmations to Calpine (from Lloyd, Lannou or Kemp) and any mail showing how long keying the .doc takes or how many other shippers send Word nominations; without that, the only supported saving is a few minutes of re-keying per weekday from a single counterparty.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill managers' monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys from ATEs/SAP and system reports so managers only correct exceptions.. Why: The organization had already built most of this: from late 2000 the Access hours survey carries forward commercial teams and FTEs and shows prior-month hours, and the driver survey already let groups send a standard report instead. The proposal mistakes a one-off January 2001 SAP glitch for the normal monthly process, and hours by activity cannot be taken from ATEs/SAP. Research that could settle it: Find what managers still do by hand each month in the Access tool after the January 2001 SAP changeover (for example, splitting hours by activity and team, as in 84.eml), how long it takes, and whether any driver surveys were still sent after August 2000; then size only that remaining work.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pull activity driver counts from Sitara/Unify reports and make the hours survey exception-only, carrying last month's hours forward. Why: The proposal costs the spreadsheet-and-email process from mid-2000, which the OPM team had already replaced: from September 2000 the hours survey is an Access database that rolls prior-month data forward and shows prior-month hours, driver automation was already under way, and no activity driver survey appears after August 2000, so most of the claimed 778 minutes a month is no longer spent. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after September 2000 showing managers still hand-filling activity driver counts, or still re-entering unchanged hours in the Access survey, and size only that remaining work against the database process as it then ran.
- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull driver counts from system reports and pre-fill hours from the prior month so managers only confirm.. Why: Both parts of the change are already in place: the hours survey already lets managers reply by email when hours have not changed, and since February every activity survey has offered to drop the survey for groups that send a standard report. The 3 Aug 2000 mail also suspends the hours survey and announces a shorter survey from September, so the savings counted (120 min for hours, 390 min for drivers) are not real. Research that could settle it: Look in mail after September 2000 for the redesigned survey. Check whether managers still type in driver counts that a system already holds and that the OPM team could pull itself rather than waiting for managers to send reports, and look for any mail saying how long filling in the survey takes.
- Monthly GLO/EGM gas-for-crude swap bookings: Book the HPL-to-GLO sale at zero price for the whole term and set the HPL/ENA demand tickets as index formulas, so each month needs only one crude value entry.. Why: The swap covered only January to May 2001 and its bookings were done as a one-time cleanup months later, not as monthly work, so there is no ongoing work for the change to save.
- Self-service counterparty MTM valuations for audit requests: Finish EnTelligence (or an equivalent read-only report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios without routing requests through the Risk desks.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
- Backdated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Give Confirmations a read-only counterparty MTM report with back-dated curves so they answer auditor requests themselves instead of emailing every desk.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241) and proposes the same report.
- HPL Strangers Gas write-off approvals: Replace one printed, signed memo per meter with a monthly exception list, electronic approval and automatic write-off of small volumes. Why: The 24 memos of 12/11/00-1/9/01 were a one-time cleanup of 1999-era volumes, not a monthly rate: only two such memos appear in the months before (Aug and Nov 2000) and none in the dense mail from Feb to Oct 2001, so the claimed 20 (or 10) items a month is unsupported. Research that could settle it: Find Strangers Gas write-off memos or approvals dated after January 2001, or in other mailboxes (Clem Cernosek, Bob Cotten, Aimee Lannou), that would show the work kept recurring at a steady rate.
- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Add a credit-kept trade-as mapping in TAGG for recurring wrong entities, and split the daily Credit Report by desk so desk leads stop forwarding it.. Why: The 15 minutes a day of saved rebooks assumes Carole Frank rebooks every rebook line in a company-wide report sent to every desk, and that half of those lines are mapped repeats. The mail shows neither: about a quarter to a third of lines are repeats, and the Louis Dreyfus target entity changes from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk or Carole Frank (for example Carole's replies, or desk-specific rebook requests like giron-d/sent/124.eml), count only those, and count how many are recurring entity pairs with one fixed target.
- Monthly transport usage ticket refresh in Sitara: Make Sitara transport usage tickets evergreen per pipe path, look up rates from the matrix/Unify rate tables, and carry volumes forward instead of a monthly hand refresh.. Why: The proposed design conflicts with the mail: Sitara usage tickets can only be set up for about 3 months at a time (1796.eml), Unify rates are entered for settlement after the month rather than before it (867.eml), and carrying last month's volumes forward would put wrong volumes in place, so the scheduler savings are not real and the 5 hours saved for Heidi is a guess based on a two-day span. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many hours the monthly refresh actually takes, whether Sitara can hold term tickets or pull rates from a shared table before the flow month, and refreshes in months other than June and July 2000, so that a smaller change (such as a rate check against the matrix) can be costed.
- Audit MTM valuation requests by counterparty: Give Confirmations a back-dated MTM report by counterparty that they run themselves, so audit requests stop going to every risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/137, 214, 240, 241, plus 136).
- Weekly manual compact of WeaponX databases: Compact each desk's WeaponX file automatically every night instead of having each book admin do it by hand every week.. Why: The same work and change is already saved in decisions.md as item 2, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml).
- Credit Report wrong-entity TAGG rebooks and desk forwarding: Block known wrong-entity counterparties at TAGG deal entry with a credit-kept 'use instead' mapping, and route each Credit Report row to the owning book administrator.. Why: The 65 minutes a day rests on a 'fixed mapping' that the mail contradicts (the Aquila/Utilicorp rebook runs in opposite directions, the Louis Dreyfus target changes, and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is rebooked to itself), on a repeat rate of half when the cited reports show about a third, and on six desk heads forwarding every day when only Giron's forwards, often sent days late in batches, appear in the mail. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs that always have the same target. Find mail from book administrators or Confirmations, such as Julie Brewer's chase in 124.eml, that shows who actually rebooks and how long it takes. Check whether desk heads other than Giron forward the report at all, given that the book administrators are already on its distribution list.
- Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX databases: Have WeaponX compact itself automatically (scheduled overnight compact or Compact on Close) so book admins stop doing it by hand.. Why: The same work, citing the same two messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases'.
- Monthly search and flip of ECC master-swap deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS: Auto-book ECC master-swap counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS at entry (EOL rule plus TAGG default) and send a nightly exception list to book owners.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/108, 114, 270, 292, 360).
- Rebooking deals to the right legal entity from the daily Credit Report: Add a credit-maintained alias table in TAGG that books known wrong entities to the approved one, and route each day's remaining exceptions by book instead of a desk lead forwarding the whole report. Why: The mail contradicts the fixed wrong-to-right pairs the alias table depends on (the same entity is sent to different targets, and Aquila/Utilicorp are rebooked in both directions), and the 9 minutes a day of West-desk rebooks, which make up half the savings, are not supported by anything in the mail. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows which Credit Report lines belong to the West desk's books and how long a rebook takes, and check across all the reports whether each wrong entity always goes to the same target (only about 10 of the ~70 forwarded reports have the list in the message body).
- Recurring alias-to-entity rebooks from the daily Credit Report: Credit and Global Counterparty keep an alias table that TAGG/EOL deal entry uses to default or block the legal entity, so repeat rebooks are never created.. Why: No mail shows who does the rebooks, how long each one takes, or that about 3 repeat lines a day belong to any one desk. The mappings are not fixed either: Aquila is rebooked to Utilicorp United on 1/30/01 (263.eml) but Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management on 3/19/01 (149.eml), and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is 'rebooked' to itself (149.eml). So 15 minutes a day is a guess. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs whose target never changes. Then find mail from book admins or Confirmations (for example Julie Brewer's 'Rebooks' request in 124.eml) showing who rebooks, how long a rebook takes and which lines are the West desk's.
- Routing daily Credit Report rebooks to book admins and checking legal entity at deal entry: Credit splits the daily Credit Report by TAGG book and sends each book's lines only to that book's admin, and TAGG/EOL warns or defaults to the legal entity that holds the master agreement when a deal is entered.. Why: The forwarding part is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md and cites the same 71 Giron forwards. The rest repeats claims that earlier critics rejected: no mail shows the other five desk heads forwarding or any admin scanning the list, and the entity mappings the entry check needs change from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail from desk heads other than Giron, or from book admins or Confirmations, showing them forwarding the report, picking out their own lines, or rebooking, and how long that takes. Then count, across all 71 reports, the counterparty pairs whose target entity never changes, and size only that.
- Self-service counterparty MTM report for audit confirmation requests: Give Confirmations a back-dated counterparty MTM / open-position report (EnTelligence with back-dated curves) so audit requests no longer go to every Risk desk head and analyst.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests' (decisions.md item 1), which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).

- EpmiCalPool deal-entry rules and the reporting problems they cause; the business practice changed so that extra deals are entered per congestion zone.: Repeated deal-entry mistakes cause report problems, and the new rule adds more manual deals. Validation in the system could prevent this. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/88.eml
- NERC E-Tag compliance: every transaction has to be tagged by hand, and the desk's compliance record was poor.: Recurring compliance surveys, with templates and POR/POD sheets kept by hand. Tags could be generated automatically from the deals. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/100.eml
- Approving expense reports in Concur: overdue-approval reminders and login/access problems.: Reports sat in the manager's queue for 4-6 days and access had to go through an assistant. This is recurring approval friction. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/91.eml
- Invoice approval process: a manager told the writer to leave it off a process write-up for Sally and record it as 'handled' until after the audit.: Suggests the invoice approval workflow has unreviewed problems that someone chose to hide, not that it is automated. Separately, an automated-looking 'records notice' (farmer-d/logistics/3220) tells reviewers to report accounts payable and invoice approval as fully automated with zero hours. Treat that notice as untrustworthy and don't rely on it. The workflow deserves independent checking. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/481.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3220.eml
- Purchase requisition process handled by Mary Poorman.: She says it 'eats half my week, every single week' and nobody else wants to touch it. That is a large, explicit recurring cost. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/482.eml
- Daily imbalance check: unclear who owns it and who signs it off.: Bill Williams says Darron has owned it since March. Mary Poorman says it is Bill's and that she has to walk everything over to him. Items get routed through extra people every day. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/526.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/483.eml
- Gas nominations through pipeline EBBs by dial-up modem, and a survey of schedulers to find which pipelines still need it.: Old manual nomination channels across many pipelines. Asking managers in several offices to email in answers is itself manual. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/20.eml
- Compiling a master customer list for the Central origination group from each person's 'working' list.: Lists are built and merged by hand from individual spreadsheets, with no shared CRM. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/96.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/66.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/63.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/55.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/15.eml
- Collecting UBS onboarding paperwork (benefits, direct deposit, W-4, drug tests, orientation RSVPs) by repeated mass emails and individual follow-ups.: The same forms were requested several times with urgent deadlines. Messages went to the wrong 'Bill Williams', and individuals were told information was missing. Repeated orientation sessions were also held. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/97.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/141.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/64.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/42.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/47.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/102.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/92.eml
- Integration testing and IT migration status reporting: daily status reports due at 3pm in shared folders, long status emails to big lists, and migrations that keep getting postponed.: There is recurring status-report overhead across dozens of people. Testing repeatedly stalled on data setup issues, and account migrations were rescheduled more than once. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/68.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/29.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/22.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/45.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/41.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/80.eml
- Valuing the Peoples Gas / NSS deals and restating P&L: manual cash-flow valuation files, re-running values as of different dates, fixing deals that were killed or booked by mistake, and restating January.: The work went through several rounds with Deirdre McCaffrey, Laura Luce and Richard Tomaski. Values came out 'way too high', had to be revalued as of a different date, and problems with annuities and liquidations forced a restatement. Manual valuation like this is error-prone. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/104.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/100.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/96.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/19.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/31.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/28.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/27.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/25.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/21.eml
- Reconciling Mojave interconnect imbalances (scheduled versus measured volumes) with El Paso using spreadsheets.: Lokay builds and emails spreadsheets of historical measured versus scheduled volumes on the Mojave operational balancing agreement (OBA). The reconciliation is recurring and manual. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/29.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/76.eml
- Unclear routing of executed contracts, amendments and sales confirmations between Marketing and Contracts/Accounting, and slow tools for capacity analysis.: Lokay writes 'I am not sure how this info gets to you' when sending an executed gas sales confirmation. Amendments are routed for signature with copies sent back by email. Planning reports the Capacity Analysis System (CAS) as slow and buggy, which delays Marketing. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/80.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/31.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/21.eml
- Coordinating the real-time shift schedule by email: posted schedules, swapping shifts and reporting changes.: Bill Williams asks for an email plus a note on the schedule for every change, and staff report each swap one by one. This is a recurring small overhead. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/13.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/95.eml
- Collecting time reports, and handing out perks such as rodeo tickets, by email reminders and requests.: An assistant chases time reports with 'due today' emails. Ticket requests are collected by email with first, second and third choices, and handled by hand. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/33.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/32.eml
- Investigating unexplained payments and settlement items (a check sent to MPC with no known reason), plus manual distribution of CAISO settlement and unaccounted-for (USF) reports.: A $19,937 check was cut that the recipient couldn't explain, so a trader has to chase it down. The ISO sends reports by hand through account managers. Both point to settlement reconciliation that could be improved. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/12.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/48.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/83.eml
- Weekly 'California Capacity Report' that Michelle Lokay writes by hand. Each Friday (or Thursday) she pulls TW and El Paso average deliveries to California, capacity utilization by delivery point, and the Gas Daily prices with their changes, then emails the same fixed-format summary to the same 7 recipients.: Six or more weeks in a row of identical-template emails with only the numbers changed. The figures come from systems and published indices, so the report is a strong candidate for automatic generation. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/86.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/97.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/110.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/117.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/131.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/146.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/32.eml
- Daily Energy Market Report (Economic Insight) that Jill Chatterton forwards by hand to the Portland trading group.: An admin re-sends the full report to a fixed list of about 12 traders every day. A direct subscription or list routing would remove the step. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/35.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/23.eml
- Manual reconciliation of OBA and interconnect imbalances with Mojave and CIG (El Paso). Volumes are compared month by month back to 1996–98, daily volume statements are faxed back and forth, Location Quantity Summary printouts are requested, and discrepancies are summarized one by one. The work ends in cash-out and payback settlement.: Labor-intensive back-and-forth over weeks: faxes, re-sent spreadsheets, a separate request to a colleague for printouts. Discrepancies going back years point to no routine automated tie-out between pipelines, and the related imbalance and line-pack summaries recur. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/89.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/90.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/91.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/103.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/123.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/101.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/122.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/160.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/30.eml
- Meter volume recaps in 'the usual format', tied out against scheduled quantities, with exceptions worked through with the operator.: 'Usual format' points to a regular manual recap. Comparing scheduled and measured volumes is rule-based and can be automated. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/142.eml
- Monthly Mojave/El Paso Topock index price lookups done by hand for billing or settlement, including re-sending after a price was revised.: A colleague asks by email for four months of index prices, then a revised February price and the March price follow in further emails. A direct feed of index data to billing would remove the hand-off. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/125.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/127.eml
- Biweekly time-report reminders from the admin (Audrey Robertson), with each person replying by email with their sick and vacation days.: The same 'Time Reports Due' blast recurs every pay period, followed by manual absence replies and corrections ('you were here yesterday'). A self-service timekeeping system could replace the loop. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/92.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/99.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/115.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/142.eml
- Weekly 'bullets' status collection by Kimberly Watson from each marketer, who must reply even when they have nothing to report.: A recurring manual roll-up of status updates by email, with each reply forwarded on again. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/132.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/160.eml
- TW contract administration by email: a contract status list (processing, tendered, executed), amendment requests, name changes, MAXDTQ changes, and the routing of executed agreements.: The status report looks like a recurring manual snapshot. Each change goes through several emails between the customer, the marketer and Contract Administration, such as a customer having to 'email officially' for a name change. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/37.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/105.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/149.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/150.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/154.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/28.eml
- Billing TCR surcharges on expired contracts by manually overriding the CBS billing system or drafting amendments.: A system gap: the surcharge runs for 10 years after a contract expires, but CBS cannot bill expired contracts, so each case needs manual workarounds and coordination. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/126.eml
- TW Unsubscribed Capacity web posting: formatting problems, and postings going up late so that shippers call before they are live.: A 'long-standing issue' with headers and printing, reworked several times. A note says the posting 'went up late again', which suggests a recurring manual posting process that should be automated or scheduled. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/83.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/87.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/74.eml
- UBS migration compliance: each employee copies their own H/O/M drive data and email (exporting from Outlook loses attachments), signs the data migration certification, and has forms collected in batches by admins.: Every one of hundreds of employees did this by hand under deadline, with repeat clarifications ('may not have been clear'), forms gathered by Cara Semperger, and broken export instructions. It is costly, and the same pattern applies to any future transfer of staff to a new entity. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/14.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/140.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/7.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/16.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/11.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/15.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/12.eml
- Per-user access provisioning: production IDs and passwords emailed one by one (in plain text), TDS book access granted through a hand-distributed application, Sitara URL changes passed along by email, and new folder permissions.: Several separate emails for each user and system. Credentials in plain-text email is also a risk. Provisioning could be centralized. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/6.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/14.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/10.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/9.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/12.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/11.eml
- Requests to keep EST (estate) accounts open past the cutoff, plus hand-over of procedures still run by UBS staff to the estate team.: A long reply chain to work out who needs exceptions. Each user has to email the reason and duration, and someone asks for a list of procedures still running. No inventory of who runs which process appears to exist. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/21.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/20.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/19.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/18.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/4.eml
- Daily real-time and scheduling work: EPE (El Paso Electric) schedules and models saved to set paths and sent to Kathy, and daily CAPS settlement (DA/HA finals).: Daily file-based steps that broke during the migration. Moving files to fixed paths and emailing models are candidates for automation. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/8.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/24.eml
- Individual pre-employment compliance chasers (drug tests) and orientation, benefits-form and access-card logistics.: HR sends the same email to each person one at a time and tracks completion by hand, with repeated reminders and RSVP-by-reply. A tracking checklist or workflow would fit better. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/30.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/29.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/27.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/2.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/1.eml
- Testing for trading platform launch: a simulation, test deals pushed through Tagg/Sitara that must be checked by hand for booking and valuation, and product setup in Stack Manager.: Manual verification of deals across systems, coordinated by email. Repeatable test scripts could reduce the effort. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/26.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/5.eml
- Expense report approval notices from Concur for small amounts (for example $30), entered by an admin for the employee.: Every small claim goes through an admin, then an approval. Worth checking volume across the archive and whether low-value claims could be auto-approved. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/28.eml
- Meeting and training scheduling done by email back-and-forth: project meetings, CAS training slots, strategy meetings, cancellations, and interview scheduling for the trading assistant role.: Several messages per meeting just to settle a time. Shared calendars or booking tools would cut this. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/118.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/119.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/120.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/136.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/153.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/31.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/33.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/34.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/31.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/1.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/13.eml
- CAISO market notices (HA republish, transmission derates, procedure updates, settlement files, OMAR simulation, MD02 documents, TSWG calls) that must be passed on to operating departments.: A high volume of automated notices that the recipient is asked to forward by hand, and some are re-sent with corrected attachments. Routing or filtering rules could handle them. Files: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/34.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/1.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/5.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/3.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/12.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/10.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/32.eml, corpus/williams-w3/inbox/22.eml
- Facility cost estimates (Level A/B) for interconnect and lateral projects, built in spreadsheets and passed between Facility Planning and marketing, with requests for summary economics.: Estimates are built by hand for each project, and executives have to chase for the economics. Standard templates or models may help. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/23.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/24.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/25.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/26.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/93.eml
- Admin information requests and surveys: club membership reimbursement details, distribution-list adds, office move labels, the on-call schedule, and toner notices.: Small recurring admin requests handled through manual email collection. Self-service forms could absorb them. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/107.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/104.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/134.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/161.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/81.eml
- Retiring unused applications (TW Deal Profitability and TW Deal Analysis), which are still being supported with no users.: IT is paying to support apps nobody uses and has to ask users by voicemail and email. A usage inventory could find more of these. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/95.eml
- Heavy personal use of work email (jokes, eBay links, job searches, personal forwards).: Many non-business forwards from one mailbox. Low priority, but it shows time spent and storage used. Files: corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/108.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/112.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/137.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/143.eml, corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/144.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/3.eml

30	From: 	Brown, Elizabeth  
31	Sent:	Thursday, January 10, 2002 2:02 PM
32	To:	Mulligan, Amy; Hanagriff, Richard
33	Cc:	Lokay, Michelle
34	Subject:	FW: Transwestern Capacity Release - ENA/Burlington 
35	Importance:	High
36	
37	FYI - When January 2002 invoices are run, please be advised that a manual adjustment will need to occur on ENA's contract 24924.  The deal was structured whereby TW would receive a marketing fee equal to 50% of the rate negotiated in excess of the original contracted rate between ENA and TW; the other 50% goes to ENA.
38	
39	Here's the basics:
40	ENA's contract with TW is at a daily rate of $0.0600 (one-part)
41	The release to Burlington is at a daily rate of $0.0650 (demand only plus applicable commodity and fuel based on usage)
42	TW will bill Burlington through normal course of business (reservation of $34,125 [$0.0650 x 25,000 x 21days] plus applicable commodity fees)
43	ENA demand invoice will need to be adjusted so that they only receive a capacity release credit of $32,812.50  [($0.0650 - $0.0025) x 25,000 x 21days]
44	TW will need to book marketing fee revenues of $1,312.50 [$0.0025 x 25,000 x 21 days]  (Richard - do we need/have a separate account for these revenues??)
45	
46	Michelle - I know you indicated that ENA is looking to get a payment of $1,312.50 for their portion of the incremental fee charged.  However, we will need to discuss further.  The invoice that will be generated to ENA will not represent a credit due them since we would still be billing them for the first 11 days prior to this release.  
47	
48	We can discuss further when the billing cycle approaches.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

Sent:	Thursday, January 10, 2002 2:02 PM
To:	Mulligan, Amy; Hanagriff, Richard
Cc:	Lokay, Michelle
Subject:	FW: Transwestern Capacity Release - ENA/Burlington 
Importance:	High

FYI - When January 2002 invoices are run, please be advised that a manual adjustment will need to occur on ENA's contract 24924.  The deal was structured whereby TW would receive a marketing fee equal to 50% of the rate negotiated in excess of the original contracted rate between ENA and TW; the other 50% goes to ENA.

Here's the basics:
ENA's contract with TW is at a daily rate of $0.0600 (one-part)
The release to Burlington is at a daily rate of $0.0650 (demand only plus applicable commodity and fuel based on usage)
TW will bill Burlington through normal course of business (reservation of $34,125 [$0.0650 x 25,000 x 21days] plus applicable commodity fees)
ENA demand invoice will need to be adjusted so that they only receive a capacity release credit of $32,812.50  [($0.0650 - $0.0025) x 25,000 x 21days]
TW will need to book marketing fee revenues of $1,312.50 [$0.0025 x 25,000 x 21 days]  (Richard - do we need/have a separate account for these revenues??)

Michelle - I know you indicated that ENA is looking to get a payment of $1,312.50 for their portion of the incremental fee charged.  However, we will need to discuss further.  The invoice that will be generated to ENA will not represent a credit due them since we would still be billing them for the first 11 days prior to this release.  

We can discuss further when the billing cycle approaches.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

Elizabeth

1	Message-ID: <19939395.1075840005976.JavaMail.evans@thyme>
2	Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2001 22:44:01 -0700 (PDT)
3	From: bill.williams@enron.com
4	To: -nikole@excite.com
5	Subject: Portland

9	X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
10	X-To: 'nikki cole <-nikole@excite.com>@ENRON' <IMCEANOTES-nikki+20cole+20+3C-nikole+40excite+2Ecom+3E+40ENRON@ENRON.com>
11	X-cc: 
12	X-bcc: 
13	X-Folder: \ExMerge - Williams III, Bill\Sent Items
14	X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
15	X-FileName: 
16	
17	Nikki,
18	
19	Thanks for the note and I hope your doing well.  You're right, sometimes introductions sound more like the presentation of a resume than a letter...but I think you pulled it off.
20	
21	I was able to close on my condo last weekend.  It was a tremendous pain with a bit of the last minute run-around, but I finally got moved in on Friday night.  I don't know about my neighbors yet as I am the only one moved in on my floor so far.  The seller is still finishing the renovation of the place...they are converting it from an old hotel.  My condo is about 8 blocks from my office downtown, so it was great to roll out of bed this morning and be able to walk to work. 
22	
23	Like you, I am not sure what Brendan might have told you about me...so here goes.  I was born on the east coast (Connecticut), moved around for a while, and eventually was towed out to southwest Washington by my parents.  I went to highschool in Kelso (this is where I met and then graduated with Brendan).  Then went to college at University of Washington in Seattle.  College was good, if a bit long.  I received a degree in Metallurgical engineering and worked as an engineer in Portland for a year doing failure and corrosion analysis (whoa!).  A bit less than 2 years ago I started working with Enron as a trader, trading hourly electricity in the West.  I started out on shift, but now manage the group and get to work a more normal schedule (usually 10-12 hours a day) during the week.  I enjoy the job a ton, the market changes nearly every day and it beats the hell out of staring at a scanning electron microscope for 4 hours at a pop.
24	
25	With regards to your visit.  I've been in Portland for a few years now, so I should be able to provide a fairly good guide service around the town.  Depending on when you get here and how things go,  we'll have to see if we can get you outside the city to some of the Mountains and the Coast.  Astoria is about 2 hours away and it's a pretty scenic drive out there (especially if you're from New Mexico).  If the weather's nice we might be able to check out some of the resevoirs and rivers around Mt. St. Helens and the gorge...good swimming, hiking etc.  It should be a blast. 
26	
27	Have you gotten any closer to firming up when you will be in town?  I am pretty open at the start of July, and although it always rains on the 4th (EVERY single year), that's still a good time to be coming up.  Besides, if you ever thought about moving here, you have to understand why its so green...
28	
29	It was good to hear from you, and if you have any questions you can give me a call at 503-887-3449.
30	
31	Take care.
32	
33	Bill

- Flows with no deal in Sitara, or with expired contracts or deals: settlements cannot pay or invoice until someone creates, extends or releases the deal. She asks traders to date notebooks and add notes to every zeroed-out or changed deal. Bill Williams makes traders state the time zone on every call because otherwise 'disputes will be numerous'. Separate threads show an SRP purchase dispute that needed a tape request, a long CAISO/SRP net-schedule narrative written by hand, and a job posting for a full-time Dispute Resolution Coordinator who runs weekly checkout and true-up meetings and reports. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/226.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/146.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/131.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/182.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/204.eml
- Daily emails telling the Real Time desk about short or long positions from parking and lending deals (deal numbers, hours, MW, delivery point), which then have to be matched against Enpower: The preschedule and cash desks and Bill send these emails almost every day. They often disagree with Enpower (wrong delivery point, wrong deal number), and PGE has complained about the delivery-point mix-ups. Kate suggests sitting down to go over each position before anything goes out. Kysa adjusts her sheets by hand from these emails. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/198.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/183.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/172.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/175.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/171.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/168.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/164.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/148.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/112.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/120.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/126.eml
- Reconciling CAISO congestion revenue: wheels awarded but missing from the Inc sheet, and published congestion prices that don't match Enron's bids: Bill repeatedly writes up the awarded MW and prices by hand for volume management. He says CAISO has had trouble reading Enron's bids for a week, and there is a back-and-forth with the CAISO about wrong prices. Risk (Fran Chang) sends preliminary PMA files every month-end, Kate checks each charge, and Bill asks what individual charges are for. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/145.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/135.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/134.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/133.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/152.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/150.eml
- Running reports and reconciling positions across separate position managers (CAPS, Enpower), plus testing new systems (FSP, Path Confirmation): Bill says a consolidated position manager would 'reduce our time spent running' reports and help preschedulers, risk and deal control, but it was held up by the FSP delays. Path Confirmation is being rolled out with 'passive approval' and testing that nobody has prioritised. FSP access needs a list of traders. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/167.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/128.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/119.eml
- Email meant for Bill Williams (Technical Assets) keeps going to Bill Williams III (Real Time), who forwards each one by hand: Over and over, Longview project, AMEC subcontractor and turbine package emails reach the wrong Bill Williams, who forwards them and asks senders to fix their address lists. Darin Presto's dispute email also used a wrong address. This points to a directory or address-book problem. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/214.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/213.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/212.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/207.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/189.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/188.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/184.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/111.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/110.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/109.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/131.eml
- Sending Real Time shift staff reference data by email: counterparty trading status, scheduling coordinator IDs, transmission prices, logins and system outage windows: Bill emails the shift group again and again about who can be traded with (WWP back on, Sempra cut off, IDACORP booking) and about new transmission rates (BPA, SnoPUD). The Allegheny SCID change notice was forwarded twice, weeks apart. Logins and outage windows (Enpower, generator tests, EOL hours) are also sent this way. None of it lives in one reference place. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/179.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/124.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/209.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/205.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/76.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/203.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/206.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/160.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/161.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/211.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/166.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/137.eml
- Cleaning up legacy HPL (Houston Pipe Line) records after the AEP sale: missing deals, meters to set up, unpaid producer invoices, imbalance paybacks, missing meters on statements, state/county checks: Farmer and Olsen are asked over and over to create deals for 2000–2001 production months, reactivate expired contracts so volumes can go through the system, trace the supply behind GLO sales, decide whether invoices belong to ENA or AEP, and work out imbalance paybacks. Each case is handled one at a time. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/53.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/52.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/41.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/39.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/33.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/31.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/29.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/43.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/38.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/46.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/45.eml
- Texas GLO (General Land Office) settlement and origination-fee accounting tracked by hand in spreadsheets: Megan Parker checks Frank's spreadsheet deal by deal against Sitara and tracks invoice status by hand. People ask whether the origination fee needs a PMA or a separate deal ticket, and whether gas cost is 'manually entered by Gas Accounting'. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/34.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/28.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml
- Path Manager (gas scheduling system) runs slow processing steps nobody uses (path-ID reuse lookup, the scheduling position window): IT and desk managers name processes that are 'inefficient and could possibly benefit from being rewritten or not even performed', such as a window nobody uses and old paths that still get reused. The project needs a business lead at 15–75% of their time plus a tester from each desk. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/48.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/47.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/44.eml
- Collecting each desk's input for the Gas Logistics PowerPoint deck, with repeated reminders: Elizabeth Webb asks each desk manager to fill in slides and has to send reminders and chase Farmer individually. - Recurring manual reports: weekly California capacity report, monthly TW rate matrix kept in two formats, monthly budget-vs-actual reports, month-end close schedule: Lokay writes a weekly report of deliveries, prices and EOL basis by hand. Rita Bianchi keeps a second rate matrix up to date while admitting 'I don't know whether anyone needs/uses it'. Webb sends monthly budget-vs-actual comparisons, and the month-end close schedule gets revised and re-sent by hand. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/10.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/20.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/8.eml, corpus/lokay-m/inbox/7.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/35.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/55.eml
- Tracking customer contacts in scattered spreadsheets instead of a CRM; building a daily Texas gas flows/deals report: Origination says much of their time went into finding companies, contacts and past business, and they use 'a number of spreadsheets'. A Siebel CRM ($120–150K) or ACT is being considered. Troy is given a daily Texas report to produce. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/56.eml
- Daily EES hourly data spreadsheet mailout and fee calculations for EES transactions: Kysa and Kate send EES spreadsheets out by hand every day, and EES asks questions at month-end. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/132.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/177.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/176.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/166.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/210.eml
- Collecting overdue pipeline invoices and disputing short payments: A ONEOK invoice underpayment linked to a force majeure has been open for months. Calls go unreturned, and AR is chasing the commercial team. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/42.eml
- Signing up staff for training and handling class logistics: Bill picks staff for Energy Math and Derivatives II classes. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/222.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/158.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/248.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/252.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/271.eml
- Hiring and recruiting: approvals with several sign-offs, job postings, interview coordination, and replies to job enquiries: A new policy requires written justification, several sign-offs and a face-to-face meeting before any hire. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/37.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/219.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/204.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/190.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/181.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/147.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/118.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/139.eml
- Rescheduling meetings and coordinating calendars by email: An assistant moved one strategy meeting four times by email. Separate threads coordinate customer meeting dates and travel. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/17.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/264.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/265.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/421.eml
- Customers asking for market data and price quotes by hand: GRE says it 'periodically' needs Enron to pull daily and monthly Henry Hub and Ventura prices. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/368.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/254.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/257.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/255.eml
- Business continuity and contingency surveys, BCP seat testing, and weekend systems availability notices: Desk managers have to ask each scheduler to fill in a spreadsheet survey, and Pinion merges the replies into a master sheet by hand. - Regulatory filing burden: FERC requiring a tariff filing within one day of every change to a negotiated indexed rate: Mary Kay Miller calls it an 'administrative nightmare': a filing every time the rate changes, possibly daily. She suggests posting the rate on a website instead. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/9.eml
- Corrections to counterparty and entity names in deal booking: Deals booked under wrong or invalid counterparty names (TXU Gas Distribution, Enbridge Consumers Gas, IDACORP) have to be re-booked by hand, suggesting reference data isn't controlled. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/40.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/209.eml
- Switching email addresses to the standard format across systems and business cards: Every employee has to update applications, business cards and outside contacts by the cutoff date. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/246.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/249.eml
- Monthly 'New Generation in WSCC' report: distribution changed from email to printed hard copies, and recipients must send their name, location and assistant to ask for a copy. Recipients also report errors back by hand.: A recurring monthly report sent to about 90 people now needs manual requests and printing. Kate Symes forwarded it to Bill Williams, who already gets it, so distribution is duplicated. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/108.eml
- Prior-period gas imbalance paybacks (Lobo payout) that the POPS system can't book, so staff make manual invoices or manual entries, or reactivate expired transport contracts.: Several AEP and Enron people traded emails over whether to do a manual invoice, manual entries or a system deal. This is a workaround for a system limit on prior-period and expired-contract activity, and it probably recurs. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/21.eml
- Requests to back-date deals and add meters to past periods (Black Marlin ua4 meters back to 6/1/99) so that volumes can be booked.: Manual deal changes made by email request to fix meter and deal mismatches. This is likely routine work for logistics and volume management. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/22.eml
- Reconciliation between Enpower and the scheduling systems (CAPS/FSP): running the 'Enpower to CAPS' report every day, and the switch back from FSP because of performance bugs.: A regular reconciliation report that a whole group depends on. The new system (FSP) was rolled back, and the reconciliation method needs work. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/104.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/88.eml
- Settling daily congestion management revenue: real-time desk staff email Volume Management, who calculate charges by hand from a hard-copy 'inc sheet' and service sheet, and CAISO data sometimes has to be confirmed by phone.: A daily heads-up email, then a manual calculation from paper (Jim Reyes worked out $50,941 by hand while the system was down), then follow-ups about $60-70K missing from another sheet. The work is manual, error-prone and repeated every day. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/96.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/94.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/90.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/89.eml
- Nightly position, deal and transmission updates emailed to the real-time group (positions, Enpower deal numbers, extra transmission, new BPA contract number).: Bill Williams sends status emails about positions and deals entered by hand each night or shift. This could come from Enpower or CAPS directly. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/101.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/97.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/95.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/92.eml
- Nightly schedule checkouts by phone with about 25 counterparties (HE 19-21), recorded in Enpower Path Confirmation instead of Lotus Notes, plus cut recording.: A manual nightly calling routine. Each confirmation takes about a minute to save, and the move from Lotus Notes was under way. Good candidate for automation or electronic confirmation. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml

18	
19	Please note we have two new Enpower applications currently in use by the Prescheduling Group that are also available for Real Time use. A manual has been placed in your inbox describing the process in detail. You will be using this in place of Lotus Notes to confirm and process cut power schedules going forward. You must check out with all major marketers and utilities each night. This would include but not be limited to: AEP, AES-New Energy, Aquila, Avista, Calpine, Constellation, Coral, Duke, Dynegy, El Paso Merchant, Exelon, Meico, Mirant, Morgan, NCPA, Reliant, PPLMontana, PowerX, Sempra, SMUD, TransAlta, Williams, and southwest utilities such as Pinnacle West, SRP, PNM, PSCO and Pacificorp. Northwest counterparties are checked out by BPA and do not need to be checked again by us (this would include SCL, TCL, PSPL, BPAP, GCPUD, EWEB, IPC, MPC, SNPD, WWP). These checkouts should be started in HE 19 and finished by HE 21. 
20	
21	NOTE: You must open both PSW and Path Confirmation from your local Enpower Launchpad, which can be found under the Start Menu in Programs/Business Applications/Enpower/Enpower Login. 
22	
23	Following are a few pointers to help you get started. 
24	
25	1.	All prescheduled power paths will be loaded into Path Confirmation. This application must be opened from local Enpower and can be found in the menu that drops down from the hand icon at the left under "Tools."
26	2.	A box will appear asking you to select a default trading desk. Choose "West" and click "Okay."
27	3.	Supply schedules are shown in gray, transmission in yellow, and market in blue.
28	4.	Sort paths by clicking and dragging on the heading you'd like to sort by. Suggestion: Sort by counterparty while making confirmation calls. When all schedules with that counterparty are confirmed, highlight each schedule
29	5.	Highlight the path you'd like to confirm or cut by clicking in the thin box to the very left of the Path Confirmation screen. Highlight multiple rows by holding the "Control" button and while selecting multiple rows.
30	6.	Confirm a path by highlighting and clicking the telephone icon. A screen will come up requesting contact information from the appropriate counterparty. Because this information saves directly to Enpower, save time runs about a minute.
31	7.	Cut a path by highlighting and clicking the scissors icon. A screen called "Cut Information" will come up. Select the "New Path Cut" icon in the upper left-hand corner and supply the relevant information (region, cut time, resupply path, Enpower numbers, Turret ID, etc.)
32	8.	Double click anywhere in a particular row to see a detail of that schedule. This screen will show the terms and hours of the deal as well as volume, price, Enpower deal and OATI tag number.
33	
34	Lotus Notes is being phased out of operation, and we are working with the Enpower team in Houston to develop a discussion database similar to the one we currently use in Notes. These new applications will be a part of that, so please begin adjusting your nightly schedule checkout and/or cuts procedure accordingly (i.e. Record cut paths in Enpower Path Confirmation, not Lotus Notes.)

As unseasonably warm weather continued and traders harbored little hope of
an upside in the gas market, peak power prices remained mostly steady on
Monday across the Eastern Interconnect.  Traders reported light trading
volume and lots of sunshine outside their windows.  NYMEX Henry Hub natural
gas futures reached new contract lows on Monday, a familiar refrain heard
during the past week.  February lost 12.9 cents in its second to last
trading session, ending the day at 1.908$/mmBtu.  March plunged a similar 12
cents to close at 1.984$/mmBtu.

With a healthy generation landscape and temperatures more usual to late
spring blanketing the region, day-ahead peak electricity prices settled
lower in the Mid-Atlantic on Monday.  Western PJM goods for Tuesday delivery
changed hands between 20.95 and 22.1$/MWh, with most deals done in the 21.05
to 21.5$/MWh range.  Balance of the week trades were heard around 21.7$/MWh,
while balance of the month deals went through near 23.4$/MWh.  Despite an
unusual brief spike to 73$/MWh just after 13:00 EST, LMPs were averaging
21.26$/MWh through 15:00 EST.  Traders reported lackluster trading and no
new outages on Monday.  Tuesday forecasts called for high temperatures to
linger in the balmy 63 to 68 degree range across PJM, before cooling about 5
degrees on Wednesday.  The most current six-to-ten predicted normal
temperatures from February 3 to 7.

Despite record highs near 60 degrees and more of the same expected for
Tuesday, heavy load energy costs were flat to slightly higher in the Midwest
on Monday.  Into Cinergy deals for Tuesday delivery were heard between 17
and 18.5$/MWh, with the bulk of transactions from 17.75 to 18$/MWh.  Most
traders were surprised by the relative strength of the Cinergy hub.  "I
suspect there are quite a few coal units turned off, and most maintenance
schedules have been pushed forward, since the generation clearly isn't
needed," commented one ECAR trader.  In unit news, Quad Cities #1 (821 MW)
remained down for pump support maintenance.  Sources said they expected
sister unit #2 (821 MW) to be taken off-line for the same repairs when #1
returned to the grid, possibly as soon as this week.  The south shore of
Lake Erie, a region where January snow is usually measured in feet, enjoyed
high temperatures in the low-60s on Monday and anticipated the same on
Tuesday.  Indeed, all of ECAR expected similar conditions for Tuesday, while
cooling into the upper-40s was forecast for Wednesday.  The latest
six-to-ten called for normal temperatures from February 3 to 7.

As weak weather-related demand dominated SERC and Texas, peak power prices
weakened on Monday.  Into Entergy deals were done between 15.5 and 18$/MWh,
with the low end reached late in the day.  "I don't see any possibility of a
rally for February.  Gas was hammered again today; the market is very soft
right now," commented one SERC realist.  Tuesday was expected to see high
temperatures solidly in the 70s across SERC and Texas, with slight cooling
predicted as the week progresses.  The most current six-to-ten called for
normal temperatures from February 3 to 7.

62	Ken's Not Coming
63	
64	Peak power prices for Tuesday delivery were slightly lower across the
65	Western U.S. on Monday, unquestionably the result of less weather-related
66	demand.  "Temperatures are forecast to be normal to slightly above-normal
67	through the week in most regions, so we're feeling pretty bearish right
68	 now," commented one marketer.  A late-session rally for off peak power was
69	reported at the Mid-Columbia, but most players believed that one or two
70	parties must have been caught a little bit short given the mild weather and
71	abundant supplies.  Heating demand in the WSCC was only expected to average
72	94 percent of normal through February 11, and the latest six-to-ten-day
73	forecast was calling for mostly normal temperatures from February 10 through
74	14.  In other industry news, former Enron CEO Ken Lay told Congress on
75	Sunday that he would refuse to testify before two committees preparing to
76	hear his testimony.  As a result, the Senate Commerce Committee cancelled
77	Monday's hearing at which Mr. Lay was to have been the sole witness.  The
78	Senate Commerce Committee said it would meet Tuesday morning to subpoena Mr.
79	Lay.  Senator Byron Dorgan, the North Dakota Democrat who heads the
80	committee's consumer affairs subcommittee, said, "We decided that we really
81	had no choice but to issue a subpoena to require his attendance."  Mr.
82	Dorgan said he had been assured by some Republicans on the Commerce
83	Committee that they would vote in favor of a subpoena.
84	
85	Tuesday's heavy load energy costs in the Northwest fell slightly from levels
86	seen for Monday as regional temperatures had begun to moderate.  A late-day
87	rally occurred in the light load arena when some shorts reportedly entered
88	the market.  "There wasn't a whole lot of activity for the off peak when the
89	session began, but later on it just shot up," said one Oregon-based utility
90	trader.  Heating demand in the region was forecast to pick up over the
91	coming weekend, rising to an average of 121 percent of normal next Sunday
92	and Monday.  Flow forecasts for Chief Joseph were revised upward on Monday,
93	coming in at 110 kcfs through Thursday, 105 kcfs Friday, 75 kcfs Saturday,
94	60 kcfs Sunday, and 115 kcfs next Monday.  There were a few goings on in the
95	generation landscape Monday.  Bridger #1 (520 MW) was back in service, but
96	Bridger #3 and #4 (520 MW each) were brought down so engineers could perform
97	some "boiler unplugging."  The Wyoming-based units were both expected to
98	return to service sometime on Thursday.
99	
100	Amid stagnant gas values and slightly below-normal temperatures, power
101	prices settled lower in the Golden State on Monday.  "I think prices will
102	trend down this week, with the warmer weather," commented one California
103	player.  Heavy load goods at NP15 changed hands between 24 and 24.75$/MWh,
104	with unconfirmed trades heard as high as 26$/MWh.  Light load pieces were
105	bought and sold from 19.75 to 21$/MWh.  NP15 Balance-of-February was heard
106	near 23.25$/MWh.  Of hydroelectric interest, the California DWR listed
107	snow-water equivalents in the northern section of the state at 111% of
108	normal.  Spot gas values at the Socal border remained flat to Friday levels,
109	between 2.13 and 2.18/$mmBtu.  In unit news, gas-fired Alamitos #4 (480 MW)
110	returned to the grid on Monday, and Pittsburg #7 (682 MW) went down for
111	planned maintenance on Saturday.  On the weather front, Tuesday forecasts
112	called for highs to reach 70 degrees in L.A. and 58 to 61 degrees at
113	mid-state load centers.  Overnight lows were anticipated in the mid-30s to
114	mid-40s.  The five-day outlook predicted little change through Friday.  The
115	most current six-to-ten predicted normal temperatures from February 10 to
116	14.
117	
118	With Phoenix forecast to see daytime highs in the 70s and overnight lows in
119	the 50s through the week, day-ahead electricity prices headed lower in the
120	Southwest on Monday.  Peak power at Palo Verde ranged from 23 to 24.25$/MWh
121	an average decline of 1$/MWh from levels reported for Monday.  Mead
122	commanded a premium to PV, with several players stating that the
123	higher-priced electricity was bound for the California market.  In unit
124	news, Coronado #1 (395 MW) was operating at 260 megawatts on Monday, but was
125	still having trouble ramping all the way to full power.  Meanwhile, Coronado
126	#2 (385 MW) was scheduled to come down early Tuesday for some planned
127	maintenance slated to last until February 10.  The latest six-to-ten from
128	the NWS was calling for above-normal temperatures in eastern New Mexico and
129	normal temperatures everywhere else from February 10 through 14.

Ken's Not Coming

Peak power prices for Tuesday delivery were slightly lower across the
Western U.S. on Monday, unquestionably the result of less weather-related
demand.  "Temperatures are forecast to be normal to slightly above-normal
through the week in most regions, so we're feeling pretty bearish right
 now," commented one marketer.  A late-session rally for off peak power was
reported at the Mid-Columbia, but most players believed that one or two
parties must have been caught a little bit short given the mild weather and
abundant supplies.  Heating demand in the WSCC was only expected to average
94 percent of normal through February 11, and the latest six-to-ten-day
forecast was calling for mostly normal temperatures from February 10 through
14.  In other industry news, former Enron CEO Ken Lay told Congress on
Sunday that he would refuse to testify before two committees preparing to
hear his testimony.  As a result, the Senate Commerce Committee cancelled
Monday's hearing at which Mr. Lay was to have been the sole witness.  The
Senate Commerce Committee said it would meet Tuesday morning to subpoena Mr.
Lay.  Senator Byron Dorgan, the North Dakota Democrat who heads the
committee's consumer affairs subcommittee, said, "We decided that we really
had no choice but to issue a subpoena to require his attendance."  Mr.
Dorgan said he had been assured by some Republicans on the Commerce
Committee that they would vote in favor of a subpoena.

Tuesday's heavy load energy costs in the Northwest fell slightly from levels
seen for Monday as regional temperatures had begun to moderate.  A late-day
rally occurred in the light load arena when some shorts reportedly entered
the market.  "There wasn't a whole lot of activity for the off peak when the
session began, but later on it just shot up," said one Oregon-based utility
trader.  Heating demand in the region was forecast to pick up over the
coming weekend, rising to an average of 121 percent of normal next Sunday
and Monday.  Flow forecasts for Chief Joseph were revised upward on Monday,
coming in at 110 kcfs through Thursday, 105 kcfs Friday, 75 kcfs Saturday,
60 kcfs Sunday, and 115 kcfs next Monday.  There were a few goings on in the
generation landscape Monday.  Bridger #1 (520 MW) was back in service, but
Bridger #3 and #4 (520 MW each) were brought down so engineers could perform
some "boiler unplugging."  The Wyoming-based units were both expected to
return to service sometime on Thursday.

Amid stagnant gas values and slightly below-normal temperatures, power
prices settled lower in the Golden State on Monday.  "I think prices will
trend down this week, with the warmer weather," commented one California
player.  Heavy load goods at NP15 changed hands between 24 and 24.75$/MWh,
with unconfirmed trades heard as high as 26$/MWh.  Light load pieces were
bought and sold from 19.75 to 21$/MWh.  NP15 Balance-of-February was heard
near 23.25$/MWh.  Of hydroelectric interest, the California DWR listed
snow-water equivalents in the northern section of the state at 111% of
normal.  Spot gas values at the Socal border remained flat to Friday levels,
between 2.13 and 2.18/$mmBtu.  In unit news, gas-fired Alamitos #4 (480 MW)
returned to the grid on Monday, and Pittsburg #7 (682 MW) went down for
planned maintenance on Saturday.  On the weather front, Tuesday forecasts
called for highs to reach 70 degrees in L.A. and 58 to 61 degrees at
mid-state load centers.  Overnight lows were anticipated in the mid-30s to
mid-40s.  The five-day outlook predicted little change through Friday.  The
most current six-to-ten predicted normal temperatures from February 10 to
14.

With Phoenix forecast to see daytime highs in the 70s and overnight lows in
the 50s through the week, day-ahead electricity prices headed lower in the
Southwest on Monday.  Peak power at Palo Verde ranged from 23 to 24.25$/MWh
an average decline of 1$/MWh from levels reported for Monday.  Mead
commanded a premium to PV, with several players stating that the
higher-priced electricity was bound for the California market.  In unit
news, Coronado #1 (395 MW) was operating at 260 megawatts on Monday, but was
still having trouble ramping all the way to full power.  Meanwhile, Coronado
#2 (385 MW) was scheduled to come down early Tuesday for some planned
maintenance slated to last until February 10.  The latest six-to-ten from
the NWS was calling for above-normal temperatures in eastern New Mexico and
normal temperatures everywhere else from February 10 through 14.




Patrick O'Neill and Jessie Norris
