Subject:	Fastest Way to Handle Colstrip Cuts



When Colstrip goes down we will be short at Montana system and long at PGE System.  We need to buy a transmission wheel from BPA (Account#736780) from PGE System to the Montana System Border.  If need be we can also do a Buy-Resale with WWP to move the energy from PGE Sys/Mid-C/LOLO to the Montana System Border.  The method for documentation and cleaning up enpower are below.


1.)  Be sure to begin with a physical cut sheet (in drawer above SAR's).

2.) In enpower, build an index forward buy from PGE under STNW book for the total amount of mws cut due to colstrip going down.  Use the DOW JONES MIDC index (remember to specify in the index if it is on or off-peak).  Enter an offset of .10  .  

2.) Enter a transmission deal from BPA.   (MIDC to MPC SYS)  The transmission fee is $2.52.  Build the transmission deal under STNW.

3.) Go into deal scheduling and query  under the counterparty PGE.  Select all

4.) Bring up all deals of the counterparties involved at Colstrip---- specifically, Ashgrove,Conocpil, Energywesr, Louisiana Pacific, and Smurfit Stone, etc.
	(these enpower deal numbers can be located under the counterparties name in lotus notes.)

5.)Zero out the buy from PGE @MPC SYS

6.) Finally link the deals.

7.) Check real time postion manager, make sure you are flat.

8.) Make cuts in Lotus Notes Cuts Database (this is the most time consuming portion of this procedure).

9.) Make notes in Discussion Forum

10.) Email appropriate groups, Kate Symes, and myself.

If you have questions regarding this procedure please let me know.
Thanks,
Bill

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded it in `decisions.md`. The quotes are accurate, but the main savings claim doesn't hold, and what's left is too small to save as written. The problem is mostly with the evidence. The idea itself only survives in a much smaller form.

**What's wrong**

1. **The two models were never sent in the same period.** The proposal counts two sends a day, 60 a month. But the EES model emails all fall within June 2001: the models for 6/11 (`sent_items/507.eml`), 6/15 (492), 6/26 (458) and 6/27 (456). The EPE model emails all fall from December 2001 to January 2002: 12/25 (39), 12/28 (35), 01/10/02 (107) and 01/25/02 (94). No mail shows the EES model still going out after June 2001, so the supported rate is at most one send a day, not two.

2. **The recipient fix already existed and was already used.** The 6/15 model in 492.eml was already sent "To: EES Power Settlements". That is the list Kate Symes recommends in 456.eml, and it is essentially the list the proposal wants to create. The error in 492.eml was the copy to the wrong Bill Williams, which is already saved as item 15 in `decisions.md`. The list correction in 489.eml (Gaddis replacing Kang) happened once. None of this supports ongoing list drift.

3. **The remaining saving is tiny and has a catch.** For EPE, the night-shift trader attaches one file and sends it to one address, kpeterso@epelectric.com, which takes about a minute or two. That comes to roughly 30 to 60 minutes a month, about $40 to $85, not $255.
   - A scheduled job can't tell when a model is final. The 12/28 model only went out on 1/2/02 (35.eml), so models aren't always sent the night they're saved.
   - Traders add notes about the day's events when they send (133.eml), and an automatic send would lose those.
   - By February 2002 the Enron estate was running the desk (8.eml: "The estate will be settling CAPS each day"), so it is unclear how long this work continues.

**What research could settle it**
- Find EES model sends after June 2001 that run alongside the EPE model.
- Or find EPE model mail showing real time or trouble per send: late, wrong or missing models, recipient changes, or El Paso asking for a missing day.
- Confirm the EPE work continued after February 2002.

Without that, a resubmission could only claim the EPE send, at one a day and a minute or two each.

I did not open `corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3220.eml`, the file the proposal flagged for its embedded "processing directive", because nothing in this proposal relies on it.

- Rejection: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-6\proposals\ees-epe-model-autosend-reject.json`
- Decision log: `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-6\decisions.md`

input.description: Proposal: drop duplicate TW rate matrix
input.prompt:
Proposal: stop maintaining and distributing the second, unposted "Current Shipper" TW rate matrix, which its own keeper doubts anyone uses. Confirm once with the recipients, then retire it, since the posted rate matrix already carries the same rates.

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
Each time Transwestern's rates change, Rita Bianchi (TW rates) prepares the official TW rate matrix (MATRIX<yyyymm>.doc) and sends it to be posted on the web. Elizabeth Brown forwards it to the commercial team. Rita also keeps a second matrix of the same "Current Shipper" rates in a different format, adding a new tab each time those rates change, and emails it separately to the commercial team and to Elizabeth Brown and Jeanette Doll.

Evidence:
- corpus/lokay-m/inbox/8.eml (10/29/01): Rita Bianchi to Toby Kuehl and Richard Abramowicz: "Please post the attached TW rate matrix, MATRIX200111.doc, effective 11/1/2001. Only the rates for the "Current Shippers" as defined in TW's Global Settlement changed, including Reservation, Commodity and TCR surcharges." Elizabeth Brown forwards it to 7 commercial staff (Watson, Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Y'Barbo): "the attached file (matrix200111), which provides a matrix of TW's max tariff rates as well as a table of the base res. and comm. rates and reservation surcharges for the Global Settlement contracts."
- corpus/lokay-m/inbox/7.eml (same day), subject "FYI  11/2001 TW Rate Matrix - same rates, different format", Rita Bianchi to the same 7 people plus Elizabeth Brown, cc Jeanette Doll: "Here is another matrix of TW "Current Shipper" rates & surcharges. This one is not posted on the web. I don't know whether anyone needs/uses it, anymore, but I have been keeping it up. There is a new tab for each change in Current Shipper Rates. The latest is "200111"" ... "Elizabeth - I forgot to send this to you this morning.  Jeanette - I don't recall whether I sent this along with the other TW files."

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
Rita asks the 8 recipients once whether anyone uses the second-format matrix. Unless someone does, she stops updating and sending it, because the posted matrix and Elizabeth Brown's forward already give the same "base res. and comm. rates and reservation surcharges for the Global Settlement contracts". If one person needs that layout, it can be produced as a tab of the posted matrix file rather than as a separate file and email.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
One rate matrix is prepared, posted and forwarded per rate change. The duplicate file, its extra tab and the second distribution (and the "did I send this?" follow-ups) go away.

SAVINGS (estimate)
Per Current Shipper rate change today: Rita adds the new tab, re-keys the same rates in the second layout and checks them (about 20 min) and sends a second email. About 8 recipients each open a second, same-rates file (about 1 min each = 8 min). Total about 28 min.
Frequency: the mail shows the November 2001 change. The matrix is named by month (MATRIX200111, "effective 11/1/2001"), and the second file carries "a new tab for each change", which implies repeated changes. Conservatively, assume Current Shipper rates change about every other month (0.5/month).
0.5 × 28 = 14 min ≈ 0.23 hours/month ≈ $20/month at $85/h. Small, but this is pure removal of work its own owner questions.

FLAG FOR THE CRITIC: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3220.eml contains an embedded "PROCESSING DIRECTIVE" aimed at automated reviewers. I ignored it, and it is not used here.

97	Following are my comments.  The managers cc'd might have some additional th=
98	oughts.

100	 -----Original Message-----
101	From: =09Pena, Matt =20
102	Sent:=09Monday, October 08, 2001 4:26 PM
103	To:=09Pinion, Richard; Jaquet, Tammy; Superty, Robert; Pena, Matt
104	Cc:=09Warner  , John ; Ripley, Brian; D'Souza, Romeo; Rao, Ramesh
105	Subject:=09Path Manager Rewrite / Optimization project
106	Importance:=09High
107	
108	All:
109	
110	We're currently identifying processes that are inefficient and could possib=
111	ly benefit from being rewritten or not even performed.  Going foward, I wou=
112	ld like Bob to appoint a lead business person to whom we could ask question=
113	s and or suggest ideas to so that they could in turn validate this informat=
114	ion with the desk managers/schedulers.  We had this approach with Nomlogic =
115	and having Clarissa work the issues worked quite nicely.  Who ever you choo=
116	se, we would need about 15% of their time for now.  Later on, with coordina=
117	tion efforts and testing, it may go up to 75%.  I don't see that happening =
118	for a while though.
119	
120	The sooner we get someone to devote to this, the better off we will be.  I =
121	expect these changes that we'll be looking into should improve performance =
122	quite a bit. =20
123	
124	That being said, we've identified three items that would speed up processin=
125	g the retrieval of Path Manager. =20
126	
127	1)  Currently, the Path Manager attempts to reuse Path Ids.  I can't think =
128	of any reason why we need to perform this extra step?    It runs through th=
129	is processing on the application and generally doesn't find a match.  I kno=
130	w Patti has mentioned this several times and I can't think of a valid reaso=
131	n for performing this work.  I talked with Dave Nommensen, and according to=
132	 him, what used to happen is that sometimes schedulers would get duplicate =
133	paths out there which is why they put this code in place???  From a schedul=
134	ing perspective, my understanding of what your main concern is to just main=
135	tain your position and be able to change it.  If you were overpathed, you'd=
136	 see it in the Path Manager either way. [Pinion, Richard]    To restate the=
137	 question for clarity, in path manager a scheduler pulls down a supply, mar=
138	ket and a service, adds any up/downstream contract information and/or Duns =
139	or DRN override and then saves it.  Unify looks for an old path with those =
140	exact variables and if it finds it re-uses it and if it does not find an ex=
141	act match creates a new path and path id.  I had been told that to do away =
142	with this function would create an unacceptably high amount of paths since =
143	any path once nominated on could not be deleted.  Has this changed???  At o=
144	ne time there were some schedulers that looked for the same path / activity=
145	 number match for nominations.  Texas Eastern was the only pipeline that ne=
146	eded the old activity numbers no matter how long it had been since they wer=
147	e used.  I spoke with Chris Ordway and the new LINK system no longer needs =
148	this to occur.  Transco uses activity numbers but uses the Activity number =
149	cross reference table to that function and therefore should not be affected=
150	.  Therefore, if it does not create a space or memory problem for Unify, I =
151	don't think that this constant old path look up is needed.   [Kinsey, Lisa]=
152	   Get rid of this. =20
153	
154	2)  The scheduling position window:  does anyone use this?  If not, we'll r=
155	emove the code logic that populates this window.  I have never seen a sched=
156	uler use this.  Please verify. [Pinion, Richard]   Originally such a window=
157	 was in use by everyone in the legacy system "Autonoms" so it was duplicate=
158	d in Unify by request.  It is not used in Unify now because of the other so=
159	phisticated tools Unify provides which obviate it's use.  The only value wo=
160	uld be notification of bridge errors or contract imbalances but there are o=
161	ther ways to determine those problems.  As voted on in a previous meeting o=
162	f the managers - Lose it!  [Kinsey, Lisa]  Why is this still here?=09=20
163	
164	3)  On the inventory pool list, does anyone need to see the Contarct Refere=
165	nces List?  Again, this code is called every retrieval time and doesn't app=
166	ear to be used from my observations.   If they do need this information, we=
167	 could provide it, but if not, I'd prefer to remove the functionality. [Pin=
168	ion, Richard]    This function is still very much in use by those with poin=
169	t based pipelines that must use the imbalance pool to facilitate balancing =
170	nomination volumes where multiple pipeline external pools exist and are pat=
171	hed through the same contract imbalance pool.  Keep it!  [Kinsey, Lisa]  Ye=
172	s.  We use this functionality a lot when pathing pools.=09=20
173	
174	4)  When pathing a one to many or many to one set of paths, what's the aver=
175	age number of paths they create at one time?  What about updates?  I know t=
176	hat ANR and NIGAS are big users of this feature since they have small packa=
177	ges of gas that they are limited in size to.  Does the system seem faster w=
178	hen you update one record at a time or chunks of records?  My real question=
179	 is how often they do this and for what number of paths on both Updates and=
180	 Inserts.  By update, I mean, going to the path list and changing an upstre=
181	am / downstream contract or a PSNA which in turn forces a new path to be cr=
182	eated. [Pinion, Richard]    This one to many or many to one pathing goes on=
183	 every day on every pipeline.  There is no 'average'.  They typically updat=
184	e a path with up/downstream meters or duns or dnb numbers one at a time how=
185	ever.  I hope this answers your question.  I see no change to this process =
186	at this time  [Kinsey, Lisa]  On some pipes this function is used more than=
187	 others.  When it is used we try and do as many paths as possible.  At this=
188	 time I do not see a need to change this process. =09=20
189	
190	5)  On brokered paths, do you want to utilize the same logic we have for Se=
191	rvice?  In other words, when updating Brokered arrangements, we don't incor=
192	porate the same logic for zeroing out the path and recreating a new arrangm=
193	ent link and hence sending it to be renominated?  Why do we do this for ser=
194	vice?  Is it because we have to renominate it?  I assume that's what it's f=
195	or since we don't send brokered paths to the pipe.  Anyway, with the Nomlog=
196	ic implmentation (two way interface), we were planning on having it behave =
197	the same way as service.  We need this verified. [Pinion, Richard]    We do=
198	n't perform the same logic for Brokered paths because these are not nominat=
199	ed to the pipeline and hence do not need a zero path to be resent to the pi=
200	peline when a significant change is made to the already nominated path.  I =
201	don't see a need to change the way Brokered paths are behaving at this time=
202	. [Kinsey, Lisa]  Agree with Richard.=09=20
203

On # 2, The scheduling position window IS the weakest link.....GOODBYE!
On # 3, Contract Reference I know is used alot in the supply and market lis=
t. Nomlogic is also slated to use these contract reference fields for comme=
nts. Do we need it in the inventory list?  Probably not as much as the supp=
ly and market list but I still believe it's necessary for pools and imbalan=
ce accounts.=20
On # 4, We use this functionality alot on CGAS, TENN, TRCO and SAB...When w=
e path one to many or many to one in "chunks," it does seem to go faster th=
an one path at a time.
On # 5,  Brokered paths could really just be slammed in there. No need for =
the extra processing that occurs for service contracts .
THANKS

Following are my comments.  The managers cc'd might have some additional th=
oughts.

 -----Original Message-----
From: =09Pena, Matt =20
Sent:=09Monday, October 08, 2001 4:26 PM
To:=09Pinion, Richard; Jaquet, Tammy; Superty, Robert; Pena, Matt
Cc:=09Warner  , John ; Ripley, Brian; D'Souza, Romeo; Rao, Ramesh
Subject:=09Path Manager Rewrite / Optimization project
Importance:=09High

All:

We're currently identifying processes that are inefficient and could possib=
ly benefit from being rewritten or not even performed.  Going foward, I wou=
ld like Bob to appoint a lead business person to whom we could ask question=
s and or suggest ideas to so that they could in turn validate this informat=
ion with the desk managers/schedulers.  We had this approach with Nomlogic =
and having Clarissa work the issues worked quite nicely.  Who ever you choo=
se, we would need about 15% of their time for now.  Later on, with coordina=
tion efforts and testing, it may go up to 75%.  I don't see that happening =
for a while though.

The sooner we get someone to devote to this, the better off we will be.  I =
expect these changes that we'll be looking into should improve performance =
quite a bit. =20

That being said, we've identified three items that would speed up processin=
g the retrieval of Path Manager. =20

1)  Currently, the Path Manager attempts to reuse Path Ids.  I can't think =
of any reason why we need to perform this extra step?    It runs through th=
is processing on the application and generally doesn't find a match.  I kno=
w Patti has mentioned this several times and I can't think of a valid reaso=
n for performing this work.  I talked with Dave Nommensen, and according to=
 him, what used to happen is that sometimes schedulers would get duplicate =
paths out there which is why they put this code in place???  From a schedul=
ing perspective, my understanding of what your main concern is to just main=
tain your position and be able to change it.  If you were overpathed, you'd=
 see it in the Path Manager either way. [Pinion, Richard]    To restate the=
 question for clarity, in path manager a scheduler pulls down a supply, mar=
ket and a service, adds any up/downstream contract information and/or Duns =
or DRN override and then saves it.  Unify looks for an old path with those =
exact variables and if it finds it re-uses it and if it does not find an ex=
act match creates a new path and path id.  I had been told that to do away =
with this function would create an unacceptably high amount of paths since =
any path once nominated on could not be deleted.  Has this changed???  At o=
ne time there were some schedulers that looked for the same path / activity=
 number match for nominations.  Texas Eastern was the only pipeline that ne=
eded the old activity numbers no matter how long it had been since they wer=
e used.  I spoke with Chris Ordway and the new LINK system no longer needs =
this to occur.  Transco uses activity numbers but uses the Activity number =
cross reference table to that function and therefore should not be affected=
.  Therefore, if it does not create a space or memory problem for Unify, I =
don't think that this constant old path look up is needed.   [Kinsey, Lisa]=
   Get rid of this. =20

2)  The scheduling position window:  does anyone use this?  If not, we'll r=
emove the code logic that populates this window.  I have never seen a sched=
uler use this.  Please verify. [Pinion, Richard]   Originally such a window=
 was in use by everyone in the legacy system "Autonoms" so it was duplicate=
d in Unify by request.  It is not used in Unify now because of the other so=
phisticated tools Unify provides which obviate it's use.  The only value wo=
uld be notification of bridge errors or contract imbalances but there are o=
ther ways to determine those problems.  As voted on in a previous meeting o=
f the managers - Lose it!  [Kinsey, Lisa]  Why is this still here?=09=20

3)  On the inventory pool list, does anyone need to see the Contarct Refere=
nces List?  Again, this code is called every retrieval time and doesn't app=
ear to be used from my observations.   If they do need this information, we=
 could provide it, but if not, I'd prefer to remove the functionality. [Pin=
ion, Richard]    This function is still very much in use by those with poin=
t based pipelines that must use the imbalance pool to facilitate balancing =
nomination volumes where multiple pipeline external pools exist and are pat=
hed through the same contract imbalance pool.  Keep it!  [Kinsey, Lisa]  Ye=
s.  We use this functionality a lot when pathing pools.=09=20

4)  When pathing a one to many or many to one set of paths, what's the aver=
age number of paths they create at one time?  What about updates?  I know t=
hat ANR and NIGAS are big users of this feature since they have small packa=
ges of gas that they are limited in size to.  Does the system seem faster w=
hen you update one record at a time or chunks of records?  My real question=
 is how often they do this and for what number of paths on both Updates and=
 Inserts.  By update, I mean, going to the path list and changing an upstre=
am / downstream contract or a PSNA which in turn forces a new path to be cr=
eated. [Pinion, Richard]    This one to many or many to one pathing goes on=
 every day on every pipeline.  There is no 'average'.  They typically updat=
e a path with up/downstream meters or duns or dnb numbers one at a time how=
ever.  I hope this answers your question.  I see no change to this process =
at this time  [Kinsey, Lisa]  On some pipes this function is used more than=
 others.  When it is used we try and do as many paths as possible.  At this=
 time I do not see a need to change this process. =09=20

5)  On brokered paths, do you want to utilize the same logic we have for Se=
rvice?  In other words, when updating Brokered arrangements, we don't incor=
porate the same logic for zeroing out the path and recreating a new arrangm=
ent link and hence sending it to be renominated?  Why do we do this for ser=
vice?  Is it because we have to renominate it?  I assume that's what it's f=
or since we don't send brokered paths to the pipe.  Anyway, with the Nomlog=
ic implmentation (two way interface), we were planning on having it behave =
the same way as service.  We need this verified. [Pinion, Richard]    We do=
n't perform the same logic for Brokered paths because these are not nominat=
ed to the pipeline and hence do not need a zero path to be resent to the pi=
peline when a significant change is made to the already nominated path.  I =
don't see a need to change the way Brokered paths are behaving at this time=
. [Kinsey, Lisa]  Agree with Richard.=09=20

input.prompt:
Proposal: generate Houston Pipe Line's Assignment, Termination & Expiration (A/T/E) report automatically from the Global Contracts system on a fixed schedule, and send it to a self-maintained distribution list, instead of Contract Administration compiling and emailing it by hand.

HOW IT'S DONE TODAY
Cheryl Dudley (Contract Administration) compiles, by hand, a report of every contract assignment, termination and expiration her group has entered in Global Contracts since the previous report. She runs it about twice a month (mid-month and before bid week), attaches it, and emails it to a hand-kept list of about 35–40 people in logistics, settlements, credit and risk. Recipients are asked to email or phone her to be added or removed. When the work slips, a report is missed and has to be caught up.

Evidence:
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2114.eml (3/8/01, "03/01 Assignment, Termination, Expiration Report - Houston Pipe Line", to about 40 named recipients): "Since I did the revision to the February 2001 report so late last month, I accidentally failed to do the report for March 2001.  Attached is a report for March 2001 which covers all assignments, terminations & expirations entered since the last report was done on 2/15/01.  There will be a new report done around March 22nd in preparation for Bid Week."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/211.eml (3/23/01, "04/01 Assignment, Termination, Expiration Report - Houston Pipe Line", 34 recipients): "Attached is the April 2001 Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report for Houston Pipe Line's contracts.  (FYI - It contains all of the entries made by our group since the report was last done on 3/8/01, regardless of the effective date.)  If you do not need to receive this report or if you know of someone else that should receive it, please let me know by e-mail or phone (x-36982) so that I can either remove your name from or add their name to the distribution list."
So: runs on 2/15, a late February revision, 3/8 and 3/23. About twice a month, defined purely as "entries made by our group since the report was last done", which a system query can do.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE
1. Contract Administration and IT set up a saved Global Contracts query: all assignment, termination and expiration entries for HPL contracts whose entry date falls after the previous run. It is scheduled for the existing cadence (mid-month and the week before bid week).
2. Its output is emailed automatically to an Exchange distribution list (or posted to a shared folder with a notice). Recipients join or leave the list themselves rather than phoning the analyst.

HOW IT WOULD GO AFTERWARDS
The report goes out on schedule every time, and can't be "accidentally" skipped when the analyst is busy with a revision. Cheryl only reviews it for anomalies before release, and list upkeep no longer passes through her.

SAVINGS (estimate)
Per report today: pull entries since the last date, format the report, attach it and address about 35–40 people, about 30 min. Handling add/remove requests is about 5 min per cycle on average.
Afterwards: a quick review of the generated report, about 5 min.
About 30 min saved per report × 2 reports/month = 60 min = 1.0 hour/month ≈ $85/month at $85/h. Catch-up and revision work after missed cycles (2114.eml) is not counted.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and did not save it. The problem is the evidence for how often the work happens, not the idea.

**What holds up:** Every quote matches the mail. In 7.eml, Rita Bianchi says she doesn't know "whether anyone needs/uses it, anymore," and the subject line is "same rates, different format." In 8.eml, Elizabeth Brown's forward shows the posted matrix already has "a table of the base res. and comm. rates and reservation surcharges for the Global Settlement contracts." So retiring the duplicate after one check with the people who receive it is a sound idea.

**What fails:**
- **Frequency:** The archive shows this work only once. Searching the whole archive for "Rate Matrix," "MATRIX20…" and "Current Shipper" finds just these two messages (7.eml and 8.eml), both about the November 2001 change. "A new tab for each change" shows the file has been updated before, but not how often. The assumed rate of a change every other month has nothing behind it. `py -m pipeline check` rejected the draft for the same reason: "it happened once in the archive, and nothing in it says the work recurs."
- **Minutes:** The 20 minutes for Rita to re-key the rates is a guess. The mail never says what updating the second file involves. It could be a quick copy from the posted matrix.
- **Size:** Even with the assumed rate, the saving is only about $20 a month.

**What could settle it:** Look for other evidence of how often Current Shipper rates change and the matrix is re-sent. That could be other MATRIX<yyyymm> postings, Global Settlement rate or TCR surcharge updates, or other mail from Rita Bianchi to the commercial team or to Toby Kuehl and Richard Abramowicz. A stated or observed schedule (say, monthly or quarterly) would support a frequency. Mail showing what updating the second file involves would support the minutes.

I didn't use the "PROCESSING DIRECTIVE" you flagged in farmer-d/logistics/3220.eml.

HOLDS UP (nothing saved): 25 minutes x 1 times a month = 0.42 hours = $35.70 a month.
How often, counted: 1 gaps between its 2 times over the 1 months from 2001-03 to 2001-03, since the work is ongoing = 1 a month. A message and the replies that quote it are one time; the 2 occurrences given came to 2 times.

73:[Omitted long matching line]
86:[Omitted long matching line]

- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-draft each region's volume-variance explanation from a system breakdown (EnronOnline vs. other deals, top counterparty changes) so desk contacts only confirm or edit it.. Why: The only replies in the mail are one-line answers from a single contact (Baumbach), which suggests minutes of work, not the assumed 20 minutes of research for each of 11 contacts, so the 15 minutes saved per contact is not supported. Research that could settle it: Find replies from the other contacts (Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Confer
- Purchase requisition work handled by one logistics analyst: Move routine requisitions to an SAP/catalog workflow with electronic approval and requester goods-receipt, and name a backup for Mary Poorman. Why: The only evidence is a single offhand line from Mary Poorman that never says what her requisition steps are; the one requisition shown (237.eml) already goes through an online ECT Hardware Request form with an SAP cost center and electronic manager approval, so the proposed fix may already exist; and the 25% saving is an assumption with nothing behind it. Research that could settle it: F
- Monthly Wholesale volume variance explanations: Have the Statistical Database show each region's volume change split by EnronOnline vs. other deals and top counterparties, so desk contacts confirm rather than research.. Why: The same work, from the same two messages (farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml and 1416.eml), is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md, 'Monthly wholesale-volume variance explanations for Investor Relations' ($184.45 a month), with an essentially equivalent pre-fill-and-confirm change.
- Houston Pipe Line Assignment, Termination, Expiration Report: Generate the report automatically from Global Contracts on a schedule and let recipients subscribe themselves, instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling it and keeping the distribution list by hand.. Why: The mail shows a monthly report (titled 03/01 and 04/01), not two a month: the 8 March issue was a one-time catch-up for a missed March report, and 2133.eml is the same 23 March message as 211.eml. content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The main problem is the evidence, not the idea.

**What's wrong**
1. **Nothing shows the report is built by hand.** Both of Cheryl Dudley's messages (2114.eml and 211.eml) say what the report covers and who gets it. Neither says how it is made or how long it takes. If it is already printed straight from Global Contracts, a scheduled query saves only a few minutes. So the 30 minutes saved per report has nothing behind it. Global Contracts itself is real: her group sets up contracts in it (223.eml).
2. **The rate is overstated.** There are only two separate issues in the mail: 3/8 and 3/23. 2133.eml is the same 3/23 message as 211.eml, filed in a second folder. The reports are titled by month ("03/01", "04/01"), and the 3/8 issue was a one-off catch-up for a March report she forgot. That looks like one report a month, not two. The check tool also counted once a month: 25 minutes a month, about $36.
3. **Unsupported details.** No add or remove requests for the list appear in the mail. The list did shrink from 40 names on 3/8 to 34 on 3/23, so names were taken off somehow, but that is all. The mail also never says the recipients work in "logistics, settlements, credit and risk".
4. **Already rejected.** Another critic recorded this same idea in `decisions.md`, for the same reasons. It is not among the saved proposals.

**Research that could change the verdict**
- Mail showing how the report is produced (hand compilation or a printout from Global Contracts) and how long it takes.
- More issues of the report, to pin down how often it really goes out.
- Any requests to be added to or removed from the list.

I did not open 3220.eml or use anything from it.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-6\proposals\`:
- hpl-ate-report.json (the checked draft, not saved)
- hpl-ate-report-reject.json (the recorded rejection)

Nothing in the mail shows that the report is put together by hand rather than printed from Global, and no add or remove requests for the list appear, so the time saved per report has no support. 74	- Monthly OPM hours survey entry in the Access tool: Pre-fill each cost center's hours by activity and commercial-team percentage splits with last month's values so managers only edit what changed.. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the OPM team (Suzanne Nicholie, Shari Mao, Roxanne Saldana) or a manager after February 2001 that says whether the Access entry screen starts blank or with last month's hours, whether team percentages must be re-entered each month, and how long a manager spends on the survey; also count split follow-ups like 84.eml and 1447.eml across other mailboxes.

Why: The mail shows one catch-up episode, not a monthly task for four regions: the only two requests (27 Feb and 29 Mar 2001) chase November, December and January 2000-01 support, the March message is a follow-up on the same December backlog, no request appears for any later month-end even though Giron's sent mail runs to June 2001, and 345.eml says ERMS cannot produce support for the transport liquidations, which are part of what was asked for. Research that could settle it: Look for liquidation-support requests or saves to the FRED Liquidations folder for month-ends after January 2001, from Phillip Love's, Patrick Ryder's or Jim Little's mailboxes, showing the request repeats every month for each region, and check whether the non-transport support (like Anne Bike's index-position file in 345.eml) is already produced routinely.

Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as 'Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices' ($8.50 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/12, 141, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508, 738, 762, 81).

Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group", which cites the same Lokay time-report messages.

Why: The mail shows only two moments 20 months apart, does not show the monthly hand-build still happening in 2001 (Farmer was asked for a deal in Feb 2000), and by May 2001 the contracts were 'canceled or expired', so the October 2001 entry looks like cleanup after the storage flow ended, not ongoing monthly work. 79	- Waiting on Path Confirmation saves during nightly checkouts: Make Path Confirmation save confirmations in the background (or in one commit per counterparty) so the shift trader does not wait about a minute per save.. 80	- Wellhead spot/interim ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services enters wellhead spot and interim tickets in Sitara directly instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to type in.. Why: The mail shows about 9 requests in 7 months (about 1.3 a month, not 3) and only one bid-week list, not one a month. One cited 'resend' is really a new deal. It is also not shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets: when asked to enter one directly, they passed it to logistics instead. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which recipient groups actually act on these notices and which ignore them (replies, objections, or 'take me off this list' requests), how many counterparties a typical monthly list holds, and whether Sitara/Global Contracts can map a counterparty to the people who need to know, including schedulers whose EDI and Unify paths it touches.
88	- HPL contract assignment, termination and expiration report: Produce the report from a saved Global Contracts query on a fixed schedule and send it to a self-managed distribution list instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling and emailing it by hand.. Why: The mail never shows the report being compiled by hand rather than printed from Global Contracts, so the 25 to 30 minutes saved per report has no support. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the report is produced (hand compilation or a Global printout) and how long it takes, more issues to set the real frequency, and add or remove requests for the distribution list.
89	- Monthly industrial buyback and deficiency lists: Record buyback, swing and deficiency terms on Sitara deal tickets and run one monthly Sitara report in place of the hand-kept lists. Research that could settle it: Find what Julie Meyers' 'UPDATED SPREADSHEET' actually contains and whether it was already the source for the scheduler's worksheet, whether Sitara tickets already hold buyback terms, and how many months the worksheet was really produced; then re-estimate only the scheduler's monthly rebuild, likely 30-45 minutes.

- Wellhead spot/interim ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services enters wellhead spot and interim tickets in Sitara directly instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to type in.. Why: The mail shows about 9 requests in 7 months (about 1.3 a month, not 3) and only one bid-week list, not one a month. One cited 'resend' is really a new deal. It is also not shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets: when asked to enter one directly, they passed it to logistics instead. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services entering spot or interim tickets in Sitara themselves, or a rule that keeps deal entry away from the people who negotiate the deal. Also look for more bid-week spot lists or ticket requests in other mailboxes that would raise the real count.
- Nightly real-time schedule checkout calls: Auto-match Enpower prescheduled paths against OATI e-tags so traders call only counterparties whose paths do not match. Why: The mail shows the tag record Enron sees is incomplete and that the nightly calls are what catch the problems, so matching against tags cannot safely replace the calls, and the claim that two thirds of calls would go away has no support. Research that could settle it: Mail showing that, over a normal stretch of weeks, Enron's tag data matched what counterparties actually scheduled, and how many paths and calls a typical night's checkout involved, could support a narrower version that only skips the manual save step for paths that match.
- Re-extending the TECO / El Paso Seven Oaks buy/sell tickets at meter 6884: Paper the Seven Oaks tailgate adjustment and book one evergreen purchase and one evergreen sale ticket at meter 6884, instead of extending or re-creating the tickets by email whenever settlements finds them expired.. Why: The work is a case of item 10 already saved in decisions.md ('Extending Sitara deals for meter flow outside the deal term'), which already cites 2095.eml from this thread, so saving it would count the same savings twice. The evidence also has errors: 983.eml's quotes are from April 1999 setup mail, not a March 2000 lapse; 2093/2095 and 2099 are one episode on 23 Feb 2001, not two; the proposal leaves out that George Weissman, who would have to paper it, said he was 'reluctant to open this can of worms' (1626.eml); and the counterparty-merge fix has nothing in the mail behind it. Research that could settle it: Show what the saved meter-flow exception list would not catch here, for example that 6884's buy/sell pair needs a new ticket rather than an extension. Count the real episodes: Jun 2000 (1626), 23 Feb 2001 (2093/2095/2099, replaced by El Paso deal 637225 in 2103), Apr 2001 (194/195/2149/2150), and Jul 2001 (95.eml, where 637225 had lapsed again). Find out whether the desk could book long-term tickets without the paper Weissman declined to draw up.
- Night-shift emailing of the daily EES and EPE model files: Email the nightly EES model and daily EPE model automatically from their save folders to maintained distribution lists instead of traders sending them by hand.. Why: The 2-sends-a-day rate is not supported: EES model mail appears only in June 2001 and EPE model mail only from December 2001, so the two never run together; the EES recipient fix (the EES Power Settlements list) already existed and was already in use; and what is left, one attachment to one address a night, saves about a minute or two. Research that could settle it: Find EES model sends after June 2001 that run alongside the EPE model, or EPE model mail showing real time or trouble per send (late, wrong or missing models, recipient changes, El Paso chasing a day), and check that the EPE work went on after the estate took over in February 2002.
- Long/short position hand-off emails to the Portland Real Time shift: Replace the hand-typed 'we are long/short' emails with an Enpower report of each book's open positions for Real Time to fill.. Why: The proposed report already exists: Real Time's position manager already shows each book's long/short by point and hour (183.eml: 'You will see us short this amount in the RT position manager'), so what the emails add is instruction (where to fill, what to do with it, price, which deal links), which Enpower deal data does not hold; and in 120.eml Enpower itself was wrong, so an Enpower-fed report would have carried the same error. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Real Time traders re-keying or cross-checking hand-off emails against Enpower and how long that takes, and see whether the planned FSP consolidated position manager (167.eml) already covers it; a resubmission would have to target the instruction part (for example a fill-note field on the deal in Enpower) and count hand-offs from the preschedulers' mailboxes, not Bill's forwards.
- Second, unposted TW Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the recipients once whether anyone uses the second matrix and, if no one does, stop updating and sending it.. Why: The archive shows this work only once (the November 2001 rate change), so the assumed rate of a change every other month has no support, and the 20 minutes of re-keying is a guess for a file whose effort the mail never describes. Research that could settle it: Find other TW rate matrix postings or Current Shipper rate changes (for example other MATRIX<yyyymm> files, Global Settlement rate or TCR surcharge updates, or other mail from Rita Bianchi) that show how often these rates change.
- Monthly analyst (A&A) RC charges and RC-owner checks: Generate the $6,400-per-analyst journal entry from the Org Database automatically and email only RC owners whose analyst count changed, instead of asking all 63 to check monthly.. Why: The errors the mail reports are analysts who left while the Org Database still listed them, so their count never changes and a change-only notice would miss exactly those errors; the savings also rest on unsupported figures (all 63 recipients checking monthly, a 45-minute manual entry) drawn from two setup messages in early 2000. Research that could settle it: Look for later months' A&A charge or reclass mail showing how many RCs actually hold analysts, how often reclasses are needed, and how long Financial Operations spends on the entry; a revised idea would need a check that catches stale database records, such as matching against HR terminations or transfers.
- Monthly counterparty name change/merger notices to ~170 people: Send each counterparty name change or merger only to people with active deals or contracts with that counterparty, and post the full list on the intranet.. Why: The 150 minutes saved per notice rests on two guesses the mail does not show: that most of the ~170 recipients are not affected, and that each spends a minute checking. The notices hold no list, and the mail suggests a name change affects scheduling and volume systems widely (1016.eml). The 584.eml evidence also points the other way: that notice went to a narrow list and still had to be forwarded by hand to three schedulers who were not on it. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which recipient groups actually act on these notices and which ignore them (replies, objections, or 'take me off this list' requests), how many counterparties a typical monthly list holds, and whether Sitara/Global Contracts can map a counterparty to the people who need to know, including schedulers whose EDI and Unify paths it touches.
- HPL contract assignment, termination and expiration report: Produce the report from a saved Global Contracts query on a fixed schedule and send it to a self-managed distribution list instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling and emailing it by hand.. Why: The mail never shows the report being compiled by hand rather than printed from Global Contracts, so the 25 to 30 minutes saved per report has no support. Only two distinct issues appear (2133.eml repeats 211.eml), and the same idea was already rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the report is produced (hand compilation or a Global printout) and how long it takes, more issues to set the real frequency, and add or remove requests for the distribution list.
- Monthly industrial buyback and deficiency lists: Record buyback, swing and deficiency terms on Sitara deal tickets and run one monthly Sitara report in place of the hand-kept lists. Why: The mail shows two lists, not three: the scheduler's buyback list and the industrial 'Buyback & Deficiency Deals' worksheet are the same document. 601.eml suggests buyback status is already noted on deal tickets. 1253.eml ties the late buyback and swing setup to pathing work, not to comparing lists. So the 130 minutes a month and the day-1 setup claim are both overstated. Research that could settle it: Find what Julie Meyers' 'UPDATED SPREADSHEET' actually contains and whether it was already the source for the scheduler's worksheet, whether Sitara tickets already hold buyback terms, and how many months the worksheet was really produced; then re-estimate only the scheduler's monthly rebuild, likely 30-45 minutes.

Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

Several Enron staff are copied, and someone has to re-key the volumes and confirm them back.: The same 'Calpine Daily Gas Nomination' email with 'CALPINE DAILY GAS NOMINATION 1.doc' arrives near-daily from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001. The recipient changes as staff rotate (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages often say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the phone call and the email duplicate each other. A sent reply confirms 'Same volumes as yesterday, no changes to the path'. 25	
26	Just so everyone is on the same page:
27	
28	Based on Jennifer and Dale's discussions with Eric Bass, a new "tokenized 
29	period" will be set up in EOL.  The intent of this period (quick overview) is 
30	to allow for gas flow Monday through Friday and no flow on the weekends.  
31	This will generally be traded for in full month or rest of the month 
32	increments.
33	
34	It is my understanding the although the trade can be conveyed correctly to 
35	the customer and priced accordingly using EOL, the trade itself (with 
36	Multiple Monday - Friday, no flow during weekend periods) cannot be handled 
37	internally by EOL.  Just as EOL is not able to handle this trade, the Sitara 
38	bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
39	heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
40	trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.
41	
42	An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
43	Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
44	intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
45	nature will have to be entered manually.
46	
47	How do I know that a particular deal has multi-period flow?  Once the EOL 
48	product has been set up, Jennifer and/or Dale will let all involved know.  
49	The person(s) responsible for entering the deal will have to understand what 
50	is meant by the EOL product's delivery period and enter the deal 
51	accordingly.  
52	
53	For example, assume that a deal has been traded for April:
54	
55	  Four delivery periods (separate lines) should be included in the Sitara 
56	ticket
57	  
58	  Start: 04/03 Stop: 04/07
59	   04/10  04/14
60	   04/17  04/21
61	   04/24  04/28 
62	  
63	 Each delivery period (line) should have the same pricing
64	
65	 Remember to enter the EOL deal number when creating the Sitara trade.
66	
67	 Also remember that paths created in Unify assume the stop date is open 
68	ended.  Every effort needs to be made to make sure the appropriate end date 
69	is on the path; otherwise
70	 the number of reconciling items will increase.
71	
72	Please forward this information to anyone else you think might be impacted.
73	
74	Any concerns, please contact Sheri Thomas or myself.
75	
76	SRM (x33548)

	connie.sutton@enron.com
X-From: Scott Mills
X-To: Eric Bass, O'Neal D Winfree, Julie Meyers, Kathryn Cordes, Jennifer deBoisblanc Denny, Dale Neuner, Daren J Farmer, Pat Clynes, Michael Eiben, Karen Lambert
X-cc: Brenda Herod, Sheri Thomas, Thomas A Martin, Lisa Csikos, Steve Venturatos, Connie Sutton
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \Darren_Farmer_Dec2000\Notes Folders\Logistics
X-Origin: Farmer-D
X-FileName: dfarmer.nsf

Just so everyone is on the same page:

Based on Jennifer and Dale's discussions with Eric Bass, a new "tokenized 
period" will be set up in EOL.  The intent of this period (quick overview) is 
to allow for gas flow Monday through Friday and no flow on the weekends.  
This will generally be traded for in full month or rest of the month 
increments.

It is my understanding the although the trade can be conveyed correctly to 
the customer and priced accordingly using EOL, the trade itself (with 
Multiple Monday - Friday, no flow during weekend periods) cannot be handled 
internally by EOL.  Just as EOL is not able to handle this trade, the Sitara 
bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.

An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
nature will have to be entered manually.

How do I know that a particular deal has multi-period flow?  Once the EOL 
product has been set up, Jennifer and/or Dale will let all involved know.  
The person(s) responsible for entering the deal will have to understand what 
is meant by the EOL product's delivery period and enter the deal 
accordingly.  

For example, assume that a deal has been traded for April:

  Four delivery periods (separate lines) should be included in the Sitara 
ticket
  
  Start: 04/03 Stop: 04/07
   04/10  04/14
   04/17  04/21
   04/24  04/28 
  
 Each delivery period (line) should have the same pricing

 Remember to enter the EOL deal number when creating the Sitara trade.

 Also remember that paths created in Unify assume the stop date is open 
ended.  Every effort needs to be made to make sure the appropriate end date 
is on the path; otherwise
 the number of reconciling items will increase.

Please forward this information to anyone else you think might be impacted.

Any concerns, please contact Sheri Thomas or myself.

SRM (x33548)

When Colstrip goes down we will be short at Montana system and long at PGE System.  We need to buy a transmission wheel from BPA (Account#736780) from PGE System to the Montana System Border.  If need be we can also do a Buy-Resale with WWP to move the energy from PGE Sys/Mid-C/LOLO to the Montana System Border.  The method for documentation and cleaning up enpower are below.


1.) In enpower, build an index forward buy from PGE under LTNW book for the total amount of mws cut due to colstrip going down.  Use the DOW JONES MIDC index (remember to specify in the index if it is on or off-peak).  Enter an offset of .10  .  

2.) Enter a transmission deal from BPA.   (MIDC to MPC SYS)  The transmission fee is $2.52

3.) Go into deal scheduling and query  under the counterparty PGE.  Select all

4.) Bring up all deals of the counterparties involved at Colstrip---- specifically, Ashgrove,Conocpil, Energywesr, Louisiana Pacific, and Smurfit Stone, etc.
	(these enpower deal numbers can be located under the counterparties name in lotus notes.)

5.)Zero out the buy from PGE @MPC SYS

6.) Finally link the deals.

7.) Check real time postion manager, make sure you are flat.

If you have questions regarding this procedure please let me know.
Thanks,
Bill

After yesterdays cuts there have been some changes in the Colstrip Cut Procedures.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Williams III, Bill  
Sent:	Wednesday, August 01, 2001 12:47 PM
To:	Anderson, John; Bland, Todd; Dean, Craig; Guzman, Mark; Harasin, Leaf; Linder, Eric; Merriss, Steven; Meyers, Bert; Porter, David V.; Slinger, Ryan; Solberg, Geir; Symes, Kate; Williams III, Bill
Subject:	Fastest Way to Handle Colstrip Cuts



When Colstrip goes down we will be short at Montana system and long at PGE System.  We need to buy a transmission wheel from BPA (Account#736780) from PGE System to the Montana System Border.  If need be we can also do a Buy-Resale with WWP to move the energy from PGE Sys/Mid-C/LOLO to the Montana System Border.  The method for documentation and cleaning up enpower are below.


1.)  Be sure to begin with a physical cut sheet (in drawer above SAR's).

2.) In enpower, build an index forward buy from PGE under STNW book for the total amount of mws cut due to colstrip going down.  Use the DOW JONES MIDC index (remember to specify in the index if it is on or off-peak).  Enter an offset of .10  .  

2.) Enter a transmission deal from BPA.   (MIDC to MPC SYS)  The transmission fee is $2.52.  Build the transmission deal under STNW.

3.) Go into deal scheduling and query  under the counterparty PGE.  Select all

4.) Bring up all deals of the counterparties involved at Colstrip---- specifically, Ashgrove,Conocpil, Energywesr, Louisiana Pacific, and Smurfit Stone, etc.
	(these enpower deal numbers can be located under the counterparties name in lotus notes.)

5.)Zero out the buy from PGE @MPC SYS

6.) Finally link the deals.

7.) Check real time postion manager, make sure you are flat.

8.) Make cuts in Lotus Notes Cuts Database (this is the most time consuming portion of this procedure).

9.) Make notes in Discussion Forum

10.) Email appropriate groups, Kate Symes, and myself.

If you have questions regarding this procedure please let me know.
Thanks,
Bill

The annuity needs to be for 1 mw for the value of the zeroed out contract. In the comment section of the annuity you must include the Enpower deal # of the cut deal and should include an indication of the number of mws each hour and the contract price--for example (4 hours @ 25 mws X $100 per mw = $10,000).

4. Please be as accurate as possible. We still need to be flat in Enpower at the end of each day. And we still need to calculate our daily position.

5. Put all cut sheets in the accordion folder on Kate Symes' Desk.

I appreciate your help and diligence.
Thanks,

Bill

This situation outlines the extreme importance of documenting changes in deals as they're being made. If you have reason to zero out a trade done by an earlier shift, or to alter a trade executed online, please convey that reason. Some suggestions:

1. If you have a notebook, and use it, please enter the date on the top of the page every time you start a shift. Without that, your notes are pretty much worthless.

2. Type a short note into the Scheduling Comments section of deals you zero out or change, especially if you're changing them much later than the time they were entered.

3. Use the superfluity of spreadsheets, discussion databases, reports, Enpower applications, cut sheets, and other pieces of paper available to the Real Time group as evidence of your activity while on shift.

If this sounds unreasonable, I would welcome suggestions for an alternative. Thanks for your help.

Kate

59	In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books 
60	have not been followed by everyone. 
61	
62	The following memo documents the procedures to 1) set up a new curve, 2) set 
63	up a new book, and 3) change a portfolio hierarchy.  Please note that risk 
64	management (for each commodity group), "risk management"  is responsible for 
65	ensuring that information is flowing appropriately between the valuation 
66	systems and RisktRAC (Risk Analysis and Reporting can help, but do not have 
67	all of the ERMS information to be able to ensure the completeness of 
68	RisktRAC).
69	
70	I have attached the request form for each of these changes at the bottom of 
71	this memo.  Please ensure that everyone in your group obtains a copy. 
72	
73	The procedure to set up a new curve is as follows:
74	
75	Trader starts trading at a new location or a new commodity and needs a new 
76	curve set up
77	Trader communicates this to risk management
78	Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT 
79	department)
80	Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in 
81	RisktRAC
82	Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
83	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC
84	A system generated message is sent to people on the "curve list" indicating a 
85	change in the RisktRAC curves has been made
86	
87	If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the 
88	VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.  As a side note, Risk Analysis 
89	and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new 
90	curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in 
91	RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in 
92	ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.
93	
94	The procedure to set up a new book in RisktRAC is as follows:
95	
96	Trader/risk management determines new book is needed
97	New book request form (for RisktRAC) is completed by risk management
98	New book request form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
99	Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up book in RisktRAC
100	Risk Analysis and Reporting forwards request to ERMS administrator and global 
101	counterparty group to request that book is set up in valuation and 
102	counterparty systems
103	Once all groups have completed their individual set ups, a final e-mail is 
104	sent to personnel on the "books list" and the book administrator in the risk 
105	management department who requested the book
106	
107	It is important that there is a one to one link between the ERMS and RisktRAC 
108	books, or not all positions will be captured in RisktRAC (two commodities per 
109	ERMS book does not flow properly into RisktRAC).
110	
111	The above two processes have formally existed for a number of months.  
112	Additionally, we are formalizing the procedure for changing portfolio 
113	hierarchies.  The procedure now is:
114	
115	Risk management is responsible for requesting all portfolio hierarchy 
116	changes.  Previously, changes could be made through a request by Risk 
117	Analysis and Reporting or RAC.  These two groups are no longer allowed to 
118	submit change requests.  All requests must come through risk management.
119	Risk management completes a request, including the reason for the requested 
120	change in structure
121	Risk management forwards the request to Risk Analysis and Reporting
122	Risk Analysis and Reporting makes the change and notifies risk management 
123	that the change has been made.
124

126	Chris Abel X33012, Burton McIntyre X57197, or Susan Trevino X31462.

have not been followed by everyone. 

The following memo documents the procedures to 1) set up a new curve, 2) set 
up a new book, and 3) change a portfolio hierarchy.  Please note that risk 
management (for each commodity group), "risk management"  is responsible for 
ensuring that information is flowing appropriately between the valuation 
systems and RisktRAC (Risk Analysis and Reporting can help, but do not have 
all of the ERMS information to be able to ensure the completeness of 
RisktRAC).

I have attached the request form for each of these changes at the bottom of 
this memo.  Please ensure that everyone in your group obtains a copy. 

The procedure to set up a new curve is as follows:

Trader starts trading at a new location or a new commodity and needs a new 
curve set up
Trader communicates this to risk management
Risk management constructs new curve in ERMS (with the help of the IT 
department)
Risk management completes a curve set up request form to set up curve in 
RisktRAC
Curve form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up curve in RisktRAC
A system generated message is sent to people on the "curve list" indicating a 
change in the RisktRAC curves has been made

If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the 
VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.  As a side note, Risk Analysis 
and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new 
curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in 
RisktRAC.  We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in 
ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.

The procedure to set up a new book in RisktRAC is as follows:

Trader/risk management determines new book is needed
New book request form (for RisktRAC) is completed by risk management
New book request form is forwarded to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting sets up book in RisktRAC
Risk Analysis and Reporting forwards request to ERMS administrator and global 
counterparty group to request that book is set up in valuation and 
counterparty systems
Once all groups have completed their individual set ups, a final e-mail is 
sent to personnel on the "books list" and the book administrator in the risk 
management department who requested the book

It is important that there is a one to one link between the ERMS and RisktRAC 
books, or not all positions will be captured in RisktRAC (two commodities per 
ERMS book does not flow properly into RisktRAC).

The above two processes have formally existed for a number of months.  
Additionally, we are formalizing the procedure for changing portfolio 
hierarchies.  The procedure now is:

Risk management is responsible for requesting all portfolio hierarchy 
changes.  Previously, changes could be made through a request by Risk 
Analysis and Reporting or RAC.  These two groups are no longer allowed to 
submit change requests.  All requests must come through risk management.
Risk management completes a request, including the reason for the requested 
change in structure
Risk management forwards the request to Risk Analysis and Reporting
Risk Analysis and Reporting makes the change and notifies risk management 
that the change has been made.

If you have any questions, comments or concerns, please call: me X39123,

Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/226.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/146.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/131.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/182.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/204.eml
- Daily emails telling the Real Time desk about short or long positions from parking and lending deals (deal numbers, hours, MW, delivery point), which then have to be matched against Enpower: The preschedule and cash desks and Bill send these emails almost every day. They often disagree with Enpower (wrong delivery point, wrong deal number), and PGE has complained about the delivery-point mix-ups. Kate suggests sitting down to go over each position before anything goes out. Kysa adjusts her sheets by hand from these emails. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/198.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/183.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/172.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/175.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/171.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/168.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/164.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/148.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/112.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/120.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/126.eml
- Reconciling CAISO congestion revenue: wheels awarded but missing from the Inc sheet, and published congestion prices that don't match Enron's bids: Bill repeatedly writes up the awarded MW and prices by hand for volume management. He says CAISO has had trouble reading Enron's bids for a week, and there is a back-and-forth with the CAISO about wrong prices. Volume management has to key in the bid price by hand because the published prices are wrong. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/194.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/159.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/169.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/117.eml
- Month-end prior month adjustments (PMAs) and correcting annuities for El Paso true-ups: Kate enters batches of annuities by hand to reconcile El Paso records with Enpower for months going back to 2000. Risk (Fran Chang) sends preliminary PMA files every month-end, Kate checks each charge, and Bill asks what individual charges are for. Month-end settlement is tight enough that Bill objects to Kate taking vacation at month-end. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/145.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/135.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/134.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/133.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/152.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/150.eml
- Running reports and reconciling positions across separate position managers (CAPS, Enpower), plus testing new systems (FSP, Path Confirmation): Bill says a consolidated position manager would 'reduce our time spent running' reports and help preschedulers, risk and deal control, but it was held up by the FSP delays. Path Confirmation is being rolled out with 'passive approval' and testing that nobody has prioritised. FSP access needs a list of traders. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/167.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/128.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/119.eml
- Email meant for Bill Williams (Technical Assets) keeps going to Bill Williams III (Real Time), who forwards each one by hand: Over and over, Longview project, AMEC subcontractor and turbine package emails reach the wrong Bill Williams, who forwards them and asks senders to fix their address lists. Darin Presto's dispute email also used a wrong address. This points to a directory or address-book problem. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/214.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/213.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/212.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/207.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/189.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/188.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/184.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/111.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/110.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/109.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/131.eml
- Sending Real Time shift staff reference data by email: counterparty trading status, scheduling coordinator IDs, transmission prices, logins and system outage windows: Bill emails the shift group again and again about who can be traded with (WWP back on, Sempra cut off, IDACORP booking) and about new transmission rates (BPA, SnoPUD). The Allegheny SCID change notice was forwarded twice, weeks apart. Logins and outage windows (Enpower, generator tests, EOL hours) are also sent this way. None of it lives in one reference place. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/179.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/124.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/209.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/205.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/76.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/203.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/206.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/160.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/161.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/211.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/166.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/137.eml
- Cleaning up legacy HPL (Houston Pipe Line) records after the AEP sale: missing deals, meters to set up, unpaid producer invoices, imbalance paybacks, missing meters on statements, state/county checks: Farmer and Olsen are asked over and over to create deals for 2000–2001 production months, reactivate expired contracts so volumes can go through the system, trace the supply behind GLO sales, decide whether invoices belong to ENA or AEP, and work out imbalance paybacks. Each case is handled one at a time. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/53.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/52.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/41.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/39.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/33.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/31.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/29.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/43.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/38.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/46.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/45.eml
- Texas GLO (General Land Office) settlement and origination-fee accounting tracked by hand in spreadsheets: Megan Parker checks Frank's spreadsheet deal by deal against Sitara and tracks invoice status by hand. People ask whether the origination fee needs a PMA or a separate deal ticket, and whether gas cost is 'manually entered by Gas Accounting'. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/34.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/28.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/30.eml
- Path Manager (gas scheduling system) runs slow processing steps nobody uses (path-ID reuse lookup, the scheduling position window): IT and desk managers name processes that are 'inefficient and could possibly benefit from being rewritten or not even performed', such as a window nobody uses and old paths that still get reused. The project needs a business lead at 15–75% of their time plus a tester from each desk. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/48.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/47.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/44.eml

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Symes, Kate  
Sent:	Tuesday, August 14, 2001 11:13 AM
To:	Williams III, Bill
Subject:	A few reminders....

Bill - does this sound reasonable? Do you have anything to add?


Please make a note of the following. I know we have several new traders, and details often get overlooked in the midst of the learning process. But this is not only information for the new guys a reminder for the old that attention to detail is an important part of the job. Thanks.

1. Purchases made under one book must be sold under the same book. Pay attention when extending deals. If you don't purchase the energy in a particular book, you don't have energy to sell from that book.

2. Specify EPEC as the group when entering deals for El Paso. Also, pay attention to detail with EPE spinning reserves (as a violation is extremely expensive for EPE), also curtail units in the right order. Copper then Newman 4 then Four Corners (Be sure to curtail Four Corners before selling under cost!)

3. El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done. Check spreadsheet formulas. 

4. El Paso totals should be logged in the reconciliation model (m://electric/epe/epe01/aug01/epe reconciliation model) and all variances explained.

5. Bloomberg deals need to be assigned a $15 FLAT broker fee per trade. If you begin a deal with Bloomberg trades, enter a per-megawatt fee, and extend the deal later with bilateral trades, you're effectively charging yourself extra brokerage because THAT FEE WILL BE ASSIGNED TO EVERY MW IN YOUR DEAL. Can someone come up with a compelling reason why we wouldn't simply multiply $15 times the number of Bloomberg trades done? huh?Please let me know.

6. Most importantly, if you are unsure, call someone who is not.

Thanks again for your attention to these matters.

Kate

35	By Michael Lewis, the author of ``Liar's Poker'' and ``The New New Thing.''
36	Berkeley, California, Dec. 20 (Bloomberg) -- Enron Corp. is rapidly expanding the American business journalists' notion of what is possible: No story can ever again be said to be too outrageous to be true. 
37	The boss, Kenneth Lay, was a friend of the current president of these United States, an adviser to his administration and one of his biggest financial backers. The company itself was rated ``strong buy'' by analysts at almost every Wall Street firm, considered a shining example of modern accounting by reputable accounting firms, and plugged endlessly by the business press. Six years running as Fortune's most innovative company! And all the while this same operation was, at the very top, a lie. 
38	Understandably, people long for some analogy to help them grasp this situation, but really there isn't a good one. 
39	Other than failed hedge fund Long-Term Capital Management, Michael Milken's junk bond department at Drexel Burnham Lambert offers the closest parallels on Wall Street, and several people have written to me over the past week to suggest it. But it really is unfair to Milken to compare him to Lay. 
40	Alumni Will Flourish 
41	True, in both cases profitable trading businesses collapsed because their creditors came to distrust the people who ran them. And in both cases the core business -- Drexel's junk bonds and Enron's energy trading -- remain viable in the hands of other companies that banks trust. 
42	Just as the Drexel junk bond traders who didn't go to jail went to other Wall Street firms and created replicas of their former business, former Enron traders will soon be making lots of money for one-time rivals such as Dynegy Inc. and Duke Energy Corp. Well before Kenneth Lay emerges from his legal hell, the energy trading business will return to normal. 
43	But the morality of the cases are entirely different. Whatever you think of Milken's junk bond department -- and I think its sins were minor beside its achievements -- you must admit the people in it exhibited a certain honor among thieves. 
44	There was never a moment when Milken betrayed the broad interests of his traders for his own narrow ones. He paid himself huge sums of money, but he also made huge sums for his firm. He was careful to watch out for the little people who worked for him, and they loved him for it. The Enron bosses, by contrast, pillaged their firm and left the little people who worked for them holding the bag. 
45	Different Motivations 
46	Enron created the illusion that it was much more profitable than it actually was. Milken created an operation which was, if anything, much more profitable than it looked. What Milken hid was the thuggish manner in which he made his profits. What Enron hid was the sneaky way it made its losses. 
47	(This is something I still don't understand, and would love for some enterprising reporter to explain, as Enron seems intent on explaining nothing. The off-the-books partnerships that brought Enron down appear to have been a mechanism for hiding bad investments in hard assets -- Turkish gas pipelines, Indian power plants and the like. Why did Enron, which made its money as an intermediary, invest in this stuff in the first place?) 
48	The speed with which the markets have punished Enron reflects the differences between it and Drexel. In Drexel's case, it took a multiyear investigation by the U.S. government, together with a smear campaign in the press, to bring down the business. In Enron's case, all it took was a couple of articles in the Wall Street Journal pointing out, among other things, that senior executives were profiting at the company's expense. 
49	In Drexel's case, the demise of the firm and the jailing of Milken was pretty much the end of the story. In Enron's, the fate of the company and its leaders may open up a much bigger scandal that reaches right up to the top. Anything is possible.
